title: Web Traffic Log Processor
spec: Create a module with several small helper functions and a main function `analyze(logs)` that processes a list of web request records. Each record has a status number, a path string, and a duration number. First, use a helper to isolate records where the status is four hundred or greater. Next, use a helper to extract the path strings from those filtered records. Then, use another helper to remove any duplicate paths from the list. Finally, use a helper to sort the unique paths alphabetically and return the resulting list. Example input: a list of three records where two have a status of four hundred. Example output: a list of two path strings.

title: E-Commerce Cart Calculator
spec: Write a small module with multiple helper functions and a main function `checkout(cart)` to process a list of shopping items. Each item has a price number, a quantity number, and a clearance boolean flag. Create a helper to isolate items that are not marked as clearance. Create another helper to multiply price and quantity for each item to get subtotals. Create a third helper that applies a ten percent discount to any subtotal greater than fifty. Finally, use a helper to sum all the calculated subtotals into a final grand total. Example input: three items where one is on clearance and one has a high price. Example output: the single numeric total cost.

title: Student Grade Analyzer
spec: Provide a module with functional helpers and a main entry function `evaluate(students)` that evaluates a list of student records. Each record contains a student identifier and a list of numeric scores. Create a helper to calculate the average score for a single student by summing their scores and dividing by the count. Create another helper to isolate students whose average score is strictly below sixty. Create a helper to extract just the identifiers of these failing students. Finally, sort the identifiers alphabetically and return them as a list of strings. Example input: two students where one has low scores. Example output: a list containing one identifier.

title: Inventory Restock Planner
spec: Build a script with small functional helpers and a main function `restock(inventory)` that determines which items need ordering. Each inventory record contains a product name, a current stock number, and a minimum required stock number. Create a helper to filter down to records where the current stock is less than the minimum required stock. Create a helper to calculate the deficit for each of these items by subtracting current stock from minimum stock. Create a helper to format these deficits into alert messages combining the product name and the deficit amount. Return the list of these alert sentences. Example input: items including apples with low stock. Example output: a list containing a sentence about restocking apples.

title: Sensor Data Smoother
spec: Implement a module utilizing small functional helpers and a primary function `smooth(readings)` to clean numerical sensor data. The input is a list of numeric measurements. Create a helper that discards any measurements below zero or above one hundred. Create another helper that computes the absolute differences between adjacent valid measurements. Create a third helper to isolate differences that are strictly greater than ten. Finally, return the count of how many such large jumps occurred as a single number. Example input: list of measurements with an anomaly and a large jump. Example output: the number one.

title: Text Word Counter
spec: Write a script with distinct functional helpers and a main function `count(text)` that processes a block of text. Create a helper to split the text into a list of individual words based on spaces. Create a helper to convert all words to lowercase. Create another helper to discard words that are exactly one character long. Create a helper that counts the frequency of each remaining word, and then extracts the counts into a list of numbers. Return the largest number from this frequency list. Example input: a short sentence with repeated long words and some single letters. Example output: the maximum count number.

title: Recipe Nutritional Calculator
spec: Create a small module containing several functional helpers and a main function `calculate(ingredients)` to determine total calories. Each ingredient record has a name, a calorie count per gram, and a weight in grams. Create a helper to discard ingredients whose name is water. Create another helper to compute the total calories for each remaining ingredient by multiplying calorie count by weight. Create a helper to sum these individual calorie totals into a grand total. Return this final numeric sum. Example input: a list with water, sugar, and flour. Example output: the numeric total calories of sugar and flour.

title: Flight Delay Tracker
spec: Develop a module with separate helper functions and a main function `track(flights)` to process airline departure data. Each flight record has a flight identifier, a scheduled departure time in minutes, and an actual departure time in minutes. Create a helper to isolate flights where the actual time is greater than the scheduled time. Create a helper to compute the delay duration for each isolated flight. Create a helper to extract the identifiers of flights that were delayed by more than thirty minutes. Return this list of flight identifiers sorted alphabetically. Example input: three flights where one is severely delayed. Example output: a list containing that one flight identifier.

title: Task Priority Sorter
spec: Build a utility with functional helpers and an entry function `resolve(tasks)` to order a list of project tasks. Each task record has a description string, a priority number, and a boolean flag indicating if it is blocked. Create a helper to discard all tasks that are currently blocked. Create a helper to extract just the description strings and priority numbers from the unblocked tasks. Create a helper to sort these extracted items descending by their priority number. Finally, extract and return just the ordered description strings as a list. Example input: three tasks where one is blocked and two are ready. Example output: a list of two description strings ordered by priority.

title: Portfolio Rebalancer Alert
spec: Write a module with several small helper functions and a main function `rebalance(assets)` to monitor an investment portfolio. Each asset record contains a ticker string, a current weight percentage, and a target weight percentage. Create a helper to compute the absolute difference between current and target weights for each asset. Create a helper to isolate assets where this difference exceeds five percent. Create a helper to format these isolated assets into warning sentences containing the ticker string. Return the list of warning sentences. Example input: a list of assets where one has drifted significantly. Example output: a list with one warning sentence.

title: Real Estate Matcher
spec: Create a script with small functional helpers and a main function `match(properties)` to find suitable homes. Each property record has a distance in miles, a price, and a square footage. Create a helper to discard properties that are more than twenty miles away. Create another helper to calculate the price per square foot for the remaining properties. Create a helper to isolate properties where the price per square foot is under two hundred. Extract and return a list of the original distances for these affordable properties, sorted from nearest to furthest. Example input: list of three properties with varying distances and prices. Example output: a sorted list of distances for the matching properties.

title: DNA Sequence Filter
spec: Implement a utility with several functional helpers and a main function `analyze(sequences)` to process biological data. The input is a list of string sequences representing DNA. Create a helper to discard any sequences that contain the letter N. Create another helper to compute the length of each remaining valid sequence. Create a helper to isolate the lengths that are exactly divisible by three. Finally, calculate and return the sum of these valid lengths as a single number. Example input: a list of three sequences where one contains an invalid letter. Example output: the numeric sum of the lengths of the valid sequences.

title: Network Packet Inspector
spec: Develop a module with distinct helper functions and an entry function `inspect(packets)` to evaluate network traffic. Each packet record contains a source address, a payload size, and a boolean flag for corruption. Create a helper to discard any packets flagged as corrupted. Create a helper to extract the payload size of each healthy packet. Create a helper to isolate payload sizes that are strictly greater than one thousand bytes. Finally, sum these large payload sizes together and return the total numeric size. Example input: several packets including a small one and a corrupted one. Example output: the total size of the valid large payloads.

title: Playlist Duration Estimator
spec: Build a script utilizing functional helpers and a main function `estimate(tracks)` to process a music album. Each track record has a title string, a duration in seconds, and an explicit boolean flag. Create a helper to discard tracks marked as explicit. Create a helper to extract the duration of each clean track. Create a helper to convert each duration from seconds into minutes by dividing by sixty. Finally, sum all the minute values and return the total estimated playing time as a single number. Example input: a list of tracks where one is explicit. Example output: the total duration in minutes of the clean tracks.

title: Extreme Temperature Finder
spec: Write a module with several functional helpers and a main function `summarize(forecasts)` to analyze weekly weather data. Each forecast record has a day name, a high temperature, and a precipitation percentage. Create a helper to discard days where the precipitation percentage is fifty or greater. Create a helper to extract the high temperatures from the remaining dry days. Create a helper to convert these temperatures from Fahrenheit to Celsius. Finally, return the maximum Celsius temperature found in the list as a single number. Example input: forecasts where the hottest day also has high rain probability. Example output: the highest temperature of the dry days.

title: Shift Availability Counter
spec: Create a small utility with functional helpers and an entry function `schedule(employees)` to analyze staffing levels. Each employee record contains a name string, a department string, and a list of available hours represented as numbers. Create a helper to isolate employees who belong to the sales department. Create a helper to count how many available hours each sales employee has by measuring the length of their hours list. Create a helper to discard any counts that are less than twenty hours. Return the number of sales employees who meet this minimum hour requirement. Example input: list of employees across different departments with varying availability. Example output: the count of qualifying sales staff.

title: Premium Room Revenue Calculator
spec: Implement a module using several functional helpers and a main function `project(rooms)` to estimate hotel income. Each room record has a category string, a nightly rate, and a boolean flag indicating if it is booked. Create a helper to isolate rooms that are successfully booked. Create another helper to discard booked rooms unless their category is premium. Create a helper to extract the nightly rate for each booked premium room. Finally, calculate the sum of these rates and return the projected total revenue as a single number. Example input: a mix of available, booked standard, and booked premium rooms. Example output: the total revenue from the premium ones.

title: Survey Score Aggregator
spec: Develop a script with functional helpers and a main function `score(responses)` to process customer feedback. Each response record has a user identifier, an age number, and a list of numeric ratings from one to five. Create a helper to discard responses where the age is under eighteen. Create a helper to calculate the sum of the ratings for each adult respondent. Create a helper to isolate sum totals that are twenty or higher, classifying them as highly satisfied. Return the count of these highly satisfied responses as a single number. Example input: three responses including a minor and an unsatisfied adult. Example output: the count of highly satisfied adults.

title: Intersection Wait Time Analyzer
spec: Build a module with distinct helper functions and a main function `analyze(vehicles)` to evaluate traffic flow. Each vehicle record contains a vehicle type string, a wait time in seconds, and a lane direction string. Create a helper to isolate vehicles in the northbound lane. Create a helper to discard any northbound vehicles that are bicycles. Create a helper to extract the wait times of the remaining vehicles. Finally, calculate the average wait time by summing the times and dividing by the count, returning this single number. Example input: northbound cars, a northbound bicycle, and southbound cars. Example output: the average wait time for northbound cars.

title: Engagement Score Calculator
spec: Write a utility with functional helpers and an entry function `evaluate(posts)` to analyze social media performance. Each post record has an author string, a number of likes, and a number of shares. Create a helper to discard posts authored by an administrator. Create a helper to compute the engagement score for each remaining post by adding the likes to double the shares. Create a helper to isolate engagement scores that are greater than one hundred. Return a list of these high engagement scores sorted from highest to lowest. Example input: posts by regular users and administrators with varying metrics. Example output: a sorted list of high scores.

title: Weekly Volume Tracker
spec: Create a small module containing functional helpers and a main function `track(exercises)` to calculate weightlifting volume. Each exercise record has a muscle group string, a number of sets, and a number of repetitions. Create a helper to isolate exercises targeting the chest muscle group. Create a helper to calculate the total repetitions for each chest exercise by multiplying sets by repetitions. Create a helper to discard any total repetition count below twenty. Finally, sum the remaining counts and return the total effective weekly volume as a single number. Example input: various exercises targeting back, legs, and chest. Example output: the total repetition volume for qualifying chest exercises.

title: Modern Fiction Extractor
spec: Implement a script with several functional helpers and a main function `extract(books)` to curate a reading list. Each book record contains a title string, a genre string, and a publication year. Create a helper to isolate books categorized as fiction. Create a helper to discard any fiction books published before the year two thousand. Create a helper to extract just the title strings from the modern fiction books. Finally, sort these titles alphabetically and return the resulting list of strings. Example input: classic fiction, modern non-fiction, and modern fiction books. Example output: an alphabetically sorted list of modern fiction titles.

title: Emissions Threshold Monitor
spec: Develop a module using distinct functional helpers and a main function `monitor(shipments)` to track environmental impact. Each shipment record contains a destination string, a distance in kilometers, and a weight in tons. Create a helper to compute the emissions for each shipment by multiplying distance by weight. Create a helper to isolate calculated emissions that exceed five thousand units. Create a helper to apply a ten percent carbon tax penalty to these high emissions values. Return the sum of all penalized emission values as a single number. Example input: three shipments with short and long distances. Example output: the sum of the penalized high emissions.

title: Leaderboard Score Processor
spec: Build a utility with small functional helpers and an entry function `update(players)` to manage a gaming tournament. Each player record contains a username, a base score, and a boolean flag for cheating. Create a helper to discard any players flagged for cheating. Create a helper to increase the base score of each honest player by a fifty point participation bonus. Create a helper to extract just the usernames of players whose new score exceeds five hundred. Return this list of successful usernames sorted alphabetically. Example input: honest and cheating players with varying scores. Example output: a sorted list of usernames for top players.

title: Defect Rate Analyzer
spec: Write a module with multiple functional helpers and a main function `analyze(widgets)` to inspect factory output. Each widget record has a batch identifier, a weight number, and a visual defect boolean flag. Create a helper to discard widgets that have a visual defect. Create a helper to check the weight of the visually perfect widgets, isolating those that weigh exactly ten units. Create a helper to extract the batch identifiers of these flawless widgets. Finally, remove duplicate batch identifiers and return them as a list of strings. Example input: widgets from different batches with some visual and weight defects. Example output: a list of unique batch identifiers producing perfect widgets.

title: Project Budget Tracker
spec: Write a function `audit(projects)` to analyze project budgets. Each project has a name, a budget, a list of expenses, and an active flag. Find all active projects. Calculate the total spent for each active project by summing its expenses. Determine the remaining budget for each by subtracting the total spent from the budget. Sort the projects by remaining budget in ascending order. Exclude any projects that have not spent any money. Check if every active project is within budget by seeing if the remaining amount is zero or greater. Find the name of the project with the highest single expense. Return a list containing the within budget boolean, the top spender name, and a list of sentences formatted as project name has remaining budget amount. For example, given a project named Alpha with a budget of one hundred, expenses of twenty and thirty, and active true, the formatted string would be Alpha has remaining budget fifty.

title: Fleet Fuel Efficiency
spec: Write a function `evaluate(vehicles)` to measure fleet efficiency. Each vehicle has a model name, a list of trip distances, and a list of fuel consumed per trip. Only consider vehicles with at least three trips. Calculate the total distance and total fuel for each vehicle. Compute the overall miles per gallon for each vehicle. Separate them into two groups based on whether their efficiency is thirty or above. Sort both groups by efficiency descending. Find the average efficiency of the inefficient group. Extract the model names of the efficient group. Return a list containing the average inefficient efficiency and the list of efficient model names. For example, a vehicle with distances fifty and fifty and fuel two and three would have an overall efficiency of twenty.

title: Subscription Churn Predictor
spec: Write a function `predict(customers)` to identify at risk accounts. Each customer has an identifier, a tenure in months, a list of recent login days ago, and a list of support ticket statuses. Filter out customers with less than six months of tenure. Count how many logins occurred in the last thirty days for each customer. Check if any support ticket status is unresolved. Flag a customer as high risk if they have fewer than four recent logins or at least one unresolved ticket. Calculate the average tenure of all high risk customers. Extract the identifiers of the high risk customers and sort them alphabetically. Return the average tenure and the sorted list of identifiers. For example, a customer with tenure ten, logins at two and forty days ago, and one unresolved ticket should be included in the high risk category.

title: Restaurant Ingredient Orderer
spec: Write a function `order(menu)` to consolidate ingredient needs. The menu is a list of dishes, where each dish has a popularity score, a vegetarian flag, and a list of required ingredients. Each ingredient specifies a name string and a quantity number. Filter dishes with a popularity score above fifty. Divide these popular dishes into a vegetarian list and a non vegetarian list. Extract all ingredients from the vegetarian dishes into a single collection. Combine the quantities for identical ingredient names into a total required per ingredient. Sort the resulting unique ingredients by total quantity in descending order. Return a list of formatted strings stating the ingredient name and its total quantity. For example, if popular vegetarian dishes require two flour and three flour, the output includes flour five.

title: Fitness Challenge Ranker
spec: Write a function `rank(participants)` to evaluate a walking challenge. Each participant has a name string and a list of daily step counts for a week. Discard participants who have missing days by ensuring the step list has exactly seven entries. Calculate the total steps for each valid participant. Identify the highest single day step count for each. Calculate the overall average steps across all valid participants. Filter out participants whose total steps are strictly below this overall average. Sort the remaining top participants by their total steps in descending order. Return a list of strings containing the name and their best day count. For example, a participant named John with seven days of one thousand steps each yields John scored best with one thousand.

title: Movie Recommendation Engine
spec: Write a function `recommend(movies)` to find top films. Each movie has a title, a genre, a release year, and a list of viewer ratings. Keep only movies released after two thousand ten. Calculate the average rating for each movie, ignoring any individual ratings below zero. Filter out movies with an average rating below four. Group the remaining movies by genre. For each genre, sort the movies by their average rating descending and select the top one. Extract the titles of these top movies. Sort the final list of titles alphabetically. Return the list of titles. For example, an action movie from two thousand fifteen with valid ratings four and five would have an average of four point five.

title: Warehouse Space Optimizer
spec: Write a function `optimize(shipments)` to manage warehouse space. Each shipment has an identifier, a dimensions array containing length width and height, and a fragile flag. Calculate the volume for each shipment by multiplying its three dimensions together. Filter out shipments with a volume of zero. Separate the shipments into a fragile list and a sturdy list. Sort both lists by volume in ascending order. Calculate the total volume of all the sturdy shipments combined. Find the fragile shipment with the largest volume. Return a list containing the total sturdy volume, the largest fragile identifier, and a list of all sturdy identifiers. For example, a shipment with dimensions ten by ten by two has a volume of two hundred.

title: Customer Review Sentiment
spec: Write a function `analyze(reviews)` to process feedback. Each review contains a username, a text body, and a star rating from one to five. Keep reviews that are exactly one star or exactly five stars. Check if the text body contains an exclamation mark. Count the number of words in each text body by splitting on spaces. Filter out reviews with fewer than ten words. Group the extreme reviews into a positive list for five stars and a negative list for one star. Sort both lists by word count descending. Extract the usernames from the negative list. Return the list of negative usernames. For example, a one star review with twelve words and an exclamation mark would have its username included in the final output.

title: Patient Medication Conflict
spec: Write a function `screen(patients)` to find medication issues. Each patient has a name, an age, and a list of prescribed medications. Each medication has a name and a list of known contraindications. Find patients who are aged sixty five or older. For each older patient, check if any of their medication names appear in the contraindications list of another medication they are currently taking. If a conflict is found, flag the patient. Count how many patients have conflicts. Create a warning string with the name of each conflicted patient. Sort the warnings alphabetically by patient name. Return a list containing the total count of conflicted patients followed by the sorted list of warnings. For example, a senior taking aspirin and warfarin where aspirin contraindicates warfarin yields a warning.

title: Sales Commission Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(sales)` to compute employee commissions. Each sale has an employee name, a product category, a sale amount, and a closed flag. Keep only the sales where the closed flag is true. Filter out sales with an amount less than one hundred. Group the valid sales by employee name. For each employee, sum their total sale amounts. Calculate their commission by taking ten percent of their total sales. Check if any employee earned a commission over one thousand. Sort the employees by commission descending. Extract their names. Return an array containing the high earner boolean and the list of names. For example, a closed sale of two hundred gives a commission of twenty.

title: Crop Yield Forecaster
spec: Write a function `forecast(farms)` to analyze crop yields. Each farm has a region name, a crop type, a list of historical yield numbers, and an active flag. Keep farms that are active. Filter out farms where the historical yield list is completely empty. Calculate the average historical yield for each farm by summing the numbers and dividing by the count. Check if any farm has an average yield strictly below fifty. Group the farms by crop type. For each crop type, find the farm with the absolute highest average yield. Sort the crop types alphabetically. Return a list containing the low yield boolean as the first element and a list of the top farm region names. For example, yields of forty and sixty average to fifty.

title: Smart Home Energy Usage
spec: Write a function `monitor(devices)` to track energy. Each device has a type name, a daily active hours number, and a wattage rating. Filter out devices that are active for zero hours. Calculate the daily watt hours for each device by multiplying active hours by wattage. Convert the watt hours to kilowatt hours by dividing by one thousand. Sum the total kilowatt hours across all devices. Find the single device that consumes the absolute most energy. Extract a list of device types that consume more than five kilowatt hours. Sort this list alphabetically. Return a list containing the total energy, the top consuming type, and the list of high consumers. For example, a device active for ten hours at one hundred watts uses one kilowatt hour.

title: Corporate Training Compliance
spec: Write a function `audit(employees)` to check training compliance. Each employee has a name, a department, and a list of completed module strings. Define a mandatory list of three specific modules containing safety, security, and ethics. Check which employees have completed all three of these core modules. Filter out those who are fully compliant. For the non compliant employees, count exactly how many core modules they are missing. Sort these employees by the number of missing modules descending, then by name alphabetically. Extract a list of strings formatted as employee name needs training. Return the formatted list. For example, an employee who only completed safety needs training for the remaining two.

title: Hotel Room Upgrader
spec: Write a function `upgrade(reservations)` to process hotel guests. Each reservation has a guest name, a loyalty tier, a booked room type, and a nights count. Keep reservations for guests in the gold or platinum loyalty tiers. Filter out reservations staying fewer than three nights. Transform the remaining reservations by changing a booked room type of standard to deluxe, and deluxe to suite, leaving other types unchanged. Check if any of these premium reservations are staying more than ten nights. Calculate the total number of nights booked by these guests. Sort the upgraded reservations by nights count descending. Extract the guest names. Return a list containing the long stay boolean, the total premium nights, and the list of guest names. For example, a gold member staying four nights in a standard room gets upgraded to deluxe.

title: Music Festival Lineup
spec: Write a function `schedule(bands)` to build a festival lineup. Each band has a name, a genre, a popularity rating, and an availability flag. Discard bands that are not available. Group the available bands by genre. For each genre, sort the bands by popularity rating descending. Take only the top two bands from each genre to form the final selections. Check if every selected band has a popularity rating above seventy. Flatten these categorized bands back into a single master list. Extract the names of the selected bands and sort them alphabetically. Return a list containing the high popularity boolean and the list of names. For example, if rock has five available bands, only the two with the highest popularity are chosen.

title: Supply Chain Bottleneck
spec: Write a function `detect(routes)` to find transit bottlenecks. Each route has a start point, an end point, and a list of transit times in days. Calculate the average transit time for each route. Filter out routes where the average transit time is strictly under five days. Calculate the reliability ratio of each route by finding its maximum transit time and dividing it by its average transit time. Check if any route has a reliability ratio greater than two. Sort the routes by this reliability ratio descending. Extract the end points of these delayed routes. Return a list containing the delayed boolean and the list of end points. For example, transit times of four, five, and nine yield an average of six and a maximum of nine.

title: Local Election Counter
spec: Write a function `tally(ballots)` to count election results. Each ballot contains a voter identifier, a district name, and a chosen candidate name. Filter out ballots where the candidate name is empty or invalid. Check if any voter identifier appears more than once and exclude all duplicate votes entirely. Group the valid unique ballots by district name. For each district, count the total votes for each candidate. Identify the candidate with the highest vote count in each district. Sort the districts alphabetically. Return a list of strings stating the district and its winning candidate. For example, if a district has three valid votes for Alice and two for Bob, Alice wins that district.

title: Podcast Episode Filter
spec: Write a function `curate(episodes)` to filter media content. Each episode has a title, a duration in minutes, a guest name, and a listen count. Keep episodes longer than thirty minutes but shorter than ninety minutes. Filter out episodes that do not have a guest name provided. Calculate the listen count per minute for each remaining episode by dividing the listen count by the duration. Find the total listen count across all these valid episodes. Check if all valid episodes have a listen rate above one hundred. Sort the episodes by the listen rate descending. Select the titles of the top five episodes. Return a list containing the total valid listen count, the high rate boolean, and the list of top titles. For example, an episode of sixty minutes with six thousand listens has a rate of one hundred.

title: Stock Portfolio Dividends
spec: Write a function `project(holdings)` to calculate investment income. Each holding has a ticker symbol, a share count, a current share price, and an annual dividend yield percentage. Filter out holdings with a share count of zero. Calculate the total value of each holding by multiplying shares by price. Calculate the expected annual dividend amount for each holding by multiplying the total value by the yield percentage and dividing by one hundred. Filter out holdings that produce less than ten in dividends. Sum the total expected dividends across all remaining holdings. Find the ticker symbol of the holding providing the largest dividend amount. Extract all valid ticker symbols and sort them alphabetically. Return an array with the total dividends, the top ticker, and the sorted symbols list. For example, one hundred shares at fifty price with a two percent yield gives one hundred in dividends.

title: Job Applicant Screener
spec: Write a function `screen(applicants)` to filter job candidates. Each applicant has a name, a years of experience number, and a list of known programming languages. Filter out applicants with less than three years of experience. Convert all programming language names to lowercase for consistency. Check if the applicant knows both javascript and python by inspecting their languages list. Keep only the applicants who possess both of these specific skills. Count the total number of languages each successful applicant knows. Sort them by total languages descending, then by years of experience descending. Extract their names. Return the list of names. For example, an applicant with four years experience knowing javascript, python, and ruby is kept.

title: Grocery Discount Applier
spec: Write a function `discount(basket)` to process grocery totals. The basket is a list of items where each item has a name, a category, a price, and a quantity. Keep items that have a quantity greater than zero. Apply a twenty percent discount to the price of items in the produce category. Apply a ten percent discount to items in the dairy category. Leave prices in other categories unchanged. Calculate the new total cost for each item by multiplying its discounted price by its quantity. Check if every item in the basket now belongs strictly to the produce category. Sum the total cost of all items in the basket. Find all items whose new total cost is over fifty. Extract their names and sort them. Return an array containing the all produce boolean, the final total cost, and the list of expensive item names. For example, a produce item originally priced at ten with quantity two becomes sixteen.

title: City Traffic Camera
spec: Write a function `monitor(cameras)` to analyze traffic violations. Each camera has a location name, a list of recorded vehicle speeds, and a speed limit. Filter out cameras that recorded zero vehicles. For each camera, count how many vehicles exceeded the speed limit by more than ten. Calculate the percentage of these severe speeding vehicles relative to the total recorded by that camera. Filter out cameras where this speeding percentage is below five. Calculate the average speeding percentage across all these severe cameras. Sort the remaining cameras by speeding percentage descending. Extract the location names. Return an array containing the average percentage and the list of location names. For example, if a camera records twenty vehicles and two are severely speeding, its percentage is ten.

title: Conference Schedule Builder
spec: Write a function `arrange(talks)` to organize sessions. Each talk has a speaker name, a track name, a duration in minutes, and an approved flag. Keep only the approved talks. Filter out talks that are longer than sixty minutes. Group the remaining talks by track name. Calculate the total duration of talks for each track by summing the individual durations. Filter out tracks that have a total duration of zero. Check if any track exceeds a total duration of three hundred minutes. Sort the tracks by their total duration in descending order. Extract the track names and sort them alphabetically. Return an array containing the long track boolean and the list of sorted track names. For example, a track with approved talks of thirty and forty minutes has a total of seventy.

title: Museum Exhibit Curator
spec: Write a function `curate(exhibits)` to organize museum displays. Each exhibit has a title, a historical era string, a list of artifact names, and an insurance value. Keep exhibits that have an insurance value over ten thousand. Filter out exhibits that have an empty artifact list. Count how many artifacts are in each exhibit. Check if any exhibit has more than twenty artifacts. Group the exhibits by historical era. For each era, sort the exhibits by their artifact count descending. Flatten the categorized exhibits back into a single sequence. Extract the exhibit titles. Return an array containing the massive exhibit boolean and the list of titles. For example, an exhibit with three artifacts and a value of twenty thousand is kept.

title: Pet Shelter Matchmaker
spec: Write a function `match(pets)` to find adoptable animals. Each pet has a name, a species, an age in months, and a list of behavioral traits. Define a list of positive traits containing friendly, calm, and playful. For each pet, check if any of their traits match the positive list. Filter out pets that do not possess any positive traits. Keep only the pets that are younger than sixty months. Sort the adoptable pets by age ascending. Extract all traits from these adoptable pets to create a summary list. Remove duplicate traits to create a unique traits list. Return an array containing the sorted adoptable pet names and the unique traits list. For example, a friendly cat aged ten months is included in the adoptable list.

title: Library Overdue Fees
spec: Write a main function `assess(records)` taking an array of book borrow records. Each record has a patron name, days kept, and a boolean for whether the book is a high demand item. Provide a helper to calculate the overdue days, which is days kept minus fourteen, returning zero if not overdue. Provide another helper to calculate the fee, which is ten cents per overdue day, plus an extra fifty cents per overdue day if the item is in high demand. Provide a third helper to format a bill string containing the patron name and the fee. The main function should filter out records that are not overdue, map the remaining records to include their computed fee, sort them by the fee in descending order, and map them using the string formatting helper to return the final list. Example: a normal book kept for twenty days yields a fee of sixty cents.

title: Marathon Runner Splits Analyzer
spec: Write a main function `analyze(runners)` taking an array of runner records. Each runner has a name, an age, and an array of split times in minutes. Provide a helper to calculate a runner's total time by summing their splits. Provide another helper to find the fastest split time for a given runner. Provide a third helper to check if a runner is a senior, meaning age fifty or older. The main function should filter for senior runners, map them to a new structure containing their name, total time, and fastest split, sort them by total time in ascending order, and extract just their names into a final returned array. Example: a fifty year old runner with splits twenty, twenty one, and twenty returns a total of sixty one and is included.

title: Space Debris Tracker
spec: Write a main function `track(debris)` taking an array of space object sightings. Each sighting has an object identifier, an orbit altitude in kilometers, and a base risk factor. Provide a helper to filter out objects with an altitude higher than two thousand kilometers. Provide another helper to calculate a scaled risk factor by dividing the altitude by one hundred and adding it to the base risk. Provide a third helper to format an alert string with the identifier and scaled risk. The main function should filter for low orbit objects using the first helper, map them to calculate their scaled risk, filter again for those with a scaled risk above fifty, sort them by scaled risk descending, and map them to the alert string. Example: an object at four hundred kilometers with base risk ten gets a scaled risk of fourteen.

title: Coffee Shop Loyalty Rewards
spec: Write a main function `reward(customers)` taking an array of customer purchase histories. Each customer has a phone number and an array of transaction amounts. Provide a helper to filter a customer's transactions to only those over five dollars. Provide another helper to count these valid transactions. Provide a third helper to check if a customer qualifies for a free drink, which requires at least ten valid transactions. The main function should map all customers to calculate their valid transaction count, filter to keep only those who qualify, sort them by their valid count descending, and map the remaining to an array of just their phone numbers. Example: a customer with twelve transactions of six dollars qualifies and their phone number is returned.

title: Freelance Invoice Totalizer
spec: Write a main function `bill(projects)` taking an array of project logs. Each project has a client name, an hourly rate, and an array of hours worked per day. Provide a helper to sum the total hours worked on a project. Provide another helper to calculate the total cost by multiplying the total hours by the hourly rate. Provide a third helper to format a string with the client name and total cost. The main function should map each project to its total cost, filter out projects that cost less than one hundred dollars, sort the remaining projects by total cost descending, and return an array using the string formatting helper. Example: a project at fifty dollars an hour with three hours worked totals one hundred fifty dollars.

title: Online Auction Bid Winner
spec: Write a main function `resolve(auctions)` taking an array of auction items. Each item has an item name, a reserve price, and an array of bid amounts. Provide a helper to filter out bids that are lower than the reserve price. Provide another helper to find the highest valid bid from the remaining amounts. Provide a third helper to check if an item received any valid bids. The main function should map each item to find its highest valid bid, filter out items that have no valid bids, sort the successful auctions by their highest bid in descending order, and map them to an array of item names. Example: an item with reserve fifty and bids of forty and sixty is resolved with a sixty highest bid.

title: Board Game Tournament Bracket
spec: Write a main function `rank(players)` taking an array of tournament participants. Each player has a nickname, a win count, a loss count, and a tiebreak score. Provide a helper to calculate the total games played by adding wins and losses. Provide another helper to calculate the win percentage. Provide a third helper to format a summary string containing the nickname and win percentage. The main function should filter out players who played fewer than five games, map the remaining to include their win percentage, sort them first by win percentage descending then by tiebreak score descending, and map them to the summary string. Example: a player with four wins and one loss has an eighty percent win rate.

title: Cybersecurity Breach Logs
spec: Write a main function `detect(logs)` taking an array of server access logs. Each log has an internet protocol address, a timestamp, and a boolean indicating success. Provide a helper to filter out successful logins, keeping only failures. Provide another helper to extract just the internet protocol address from a log entry. Provide a third helper to format a string marking an address as suspicious. The main function should filter for failed logins, map them to their addresses, filter to keep only addresses that start with the number ten, sort the addresses alphabetically, and map them to the suspicious marker string. Example: a failed login from ten point zero point zero point one is flagged and formatted.

title: Plant Watering Schedule
spec: Write a main function `schedule(plants)` taking an array of houseplant profiles. Each plant has a species, a last watered day represented as an integer, and a watering frequency in days. Provide a helper to calculate the next required watering day by adding the frequency to the last watered day. Provide another helper to check if a plant needs watering on or before day thirty. Provide a third helper to format a string stating the species and the required day. The main function should map the plants to include their next watering day, filter for those needing water by day thirty, sort them by the next watering day ascending, and map them to the formatted strings. Example: a fern last watered on day ten with a frequency of seven needs water on day seventeen.

title: Cryptocurrency Trade Taxes
spec: Write a main function `assess(trades)` taking an array of digital currency transactions. Each transaction has an asset name, a buy price, a sell price, and a quantity. Provide a helper to calculate the profit of a single transaction by subtracting the buy price from the sell price and multiplying by the quantity. Provide another helper to filter out transactions that resulted in a loss or zero profit. Provide a third helper to compute a flat tax of twenty percent on a given profit amount. The main function should filter for profitable trades, map them to calculate their tax owed, sort them by tax owed descending, and map them to an array of asset names. Example: a trade buying at ten and selling at fifteen with quantity two owes a tax of two.

title: Charity Donation Milestones
spec: Write a main function `track(campaigns)` taking an array of fundraising campaigns. Each campaign has a cause, a target goal, and an array of individual donation amounts. Provide a helper to sum the donations for a campaign. Provide another helper to calculate the percentage of the goal reached. Provide a third helper to check if a campaign is fully funded, meaning it reached at least one hundred percent. The main function should map each campaign to its funded percentage, filter to keep only the fully funded ones, sort them by percentage descending, and map them to an array of their causes. Example: a campaign for wildlife with a target of five hundred and donations totaling six hundred is fully funded at one hundred twenty percent.

title: Smart Parking Meter Billing
spec: Write a main function `bill(sessions)` taking an array of parking sessions. Each session has a license plate, a premium flag, and minutes parked. Provide a helper to determine the hourly rate, which is two dollars for standard and five dollars for premium. Provide another helper to calculate the total charge by multiplying the rate by the hours parked, calculated by dividing minutes by sixty. Provide a third helper to check if a session lasted more than fifteen minutes. The main function should filter out short free sessions, map the remaining to their total charge, sort the sessions by charge descending, and map them to a formatted string with the license plate and charge. Example: sixty minutes in a standard zone charges two dollars.

title: Astronomy Star Catalog
spec: Write a main function `catalog(stars)` taking an array of star observations. Each observation has a star designation, a distance in light years, and an apparent magnitude. Provide a helper to calculate absolute magnitude using apparent magnitude minus five times the base ten logarithm of the distance divided by ten. Provide another helper to check if a star is closer than one thousand light years. Provide a third helper to classify a star as bright if its absolute magnitude is less than zero. The main function should filter for nearby stars, map them to calculate their absolute magnitude, filter again for bright stars, sort them by absolute magnitude ascending, and map them to their designations. Example: a star with apparent magnitude two and distance ten has an absolute magnitude of two.

title: Language Flashcard Stats
spec: Write a main function `evaluate(decks)` taking an array of study decks. Each deck has a language name and an array of boolean card results indicating correctness. Provide a helper to count the number of correct answers in a deck. Provide another helper to calculate the accuracy percentage. Provide a third helper to check if a deck has at least twenty cards. The main function should filter for decks with enough cards, map them to calculate their accuracy, filter for those with accuracy above seventy percent, sort them by accuracy descending, and map them to the language name. Example: a deck with twenty cards and fifteen correct answers has an accuracy of seventy five.

title: Dietary Macro Breakdown
spec: Write a main function `analyze(meals)` taking an array of food logs. Each meal has a food name, grams of protein, grams of carbohydrates, and grams of fat. Provide a helper to calculate total calories for a meal by multiplying protein and carbs by four, and fat by nine. Provide another helper to check if a meal is under five hundred calories. Provide a third helper to determine if a meal is high protein, meaning protein calories are more than thirty percent of the total. The main function should map the meals to their total calories, filter for low calorie meals, filter again for high protein meals, sort them by total calories ascending, and map them to their food names. Example: a meal with thirty protein, twenty carbs, and five fat has two hundred forty five calories and is high protein.

title: Volunteer Shift Scheduler
spec: Write a main function `schedule(volunteers)` taking an array of volunteer availabilities. Each volunteer has a name, a preferred role, and an array of available weekdays. Provide a helper to check if a volunteer is available on Saturday. Provide another helper to check if a volunteer prefers the role of guide. Provide a third helper to count the total number of days a volunteer is available. The main function should filter for Saturday available volunteers, filter again for those wanting the guide role, map them to calculate their total available days, sort them by days descending, and map them to their names. Example: a volunteer available three days including Saturday who wants to be a guide is included.

title: Escape Room Leaderboard
spec: Write a main function `rank(teams)` taking an array of escape room attempts. Each team has a team name, a completion status, time taken in seconds, and a hint used boolean. Provide a helper to filter out teams that did not complete the room. Provide another helper to calculate the final time by adding sixty seconds if they used a hint. Provide a third helper to format a string containing the team name and final time. The main function should filter for successful teams, map them to calculate their penalized time, filter out times longer than three thousand seconds, sort them by final time ascending, and map them using the formatting helper. Example: a team escaping in one hundred thirty seconds with a hint gets a final time of one hundred ninety.

title: Ocean Tide Predictor
spec: Write a main function `predict(stations)` taking an array of tide monitoring stations. Each station has a location name, a base tide level, and an array of hourly wave height readings. Provide a helper to calculate the average wave height for a station. Provide another helper to determine the peak tide level by adding the average wave height to the base tide. Provide a third helper to check if the peak tide exceeds five meters. The main function should map each station to its peak tide, filter for those with high tides, sort them by peak tide descending, and map them to an array of location names. Example: a base of two and an average wave of four yields a peak tide of six.

title: Ride Share Fare Split
spec: Write a main function `split(rides)` taking an array of shared trips. Each trip has a total distance in miles, a base fare, and a rider count. Provide a helper to calculate the total trip cost by adding two dollars per mile to the base fare. Provide another helper to calculate the cost per rider by dividing the total cost by the rider count. Provide a third helper to check if a trip had more than one rider. The main function should filter for shared trips, map them to their cost per rider, filter out trips where the per rider cost is less than five dollars, sort the trips by this cost descending, and map them to a formatted string showing the distance and per rider cost. Example: a ten mile trip with a five dollar base and two riders costs twelve dollars and fifty cents per rider.

title: Concert Scalper Detector
spec: Write a main function `detect(purchases)` taking an array of ticket sales. Each sale has a buyer email, a purchase timestamp, and ticket quantity. Provide a helper to extract the domain from the buyer email. Provide another helper to check if a purchase was for more than eight tickets. Provide a third helper to format a warning string with the domain and ticket quantity. The main function should filter for excessive purchases, map them to extract the email domain, filter to keep domains that end in dot com, sort the purchases by ticket quantity descending, and map them to the warning strings. Example: an excessive purchase of ten tickets by generic mail dot com triggers a formatted warning.

title: Blood Donation Eligibility
spec: Write a main function `screen(donors)` taking an array of donor profiles. Each donor has a name, a weight in kilograms, a last donation day integer, and an iron level. Provide a helper to check if a donor weighs at least fifty kilograms. Provide another helper to check if a donor donated more than fifty six days ago. Provide a third helper to check if the iron level is above twelve point five. The main function should filter using the weight helper, filter using the days helper, filter using the iron helper, sort the remaining eligible donors alphabetically by name, and map them to return just the array of names. Example: a donor weighing sixty kilograms who donated sixty days ago with an iron level of thirteen is eligible.

title: Gymnastics Routine Scorer
spec: Write a main function `score(routines)` taking an array of gymnast performances. Each performance has a gymnast name, a base difficulty value, and an array of five execution scores from judges. Provide a helper to sort a copy of the scores array and drop the highest and lowest values. Provide another helper to average the remaining three execution scores. Provide a third helper to calculate the final score by adding the base difficulty to the execution average. The main function should map the routines to calculate their final score, filter out routines with a final score below fourteen, sort them by final score descending, and map them to an array of gymnast names. Example: base difficulty six with execution scores of eight, eight, eight, nine, and seven yields a final score of fourteen.

title: Drone Delivery Path
spec: Write a main function `route(deliveries)` taking an array of package destinations. Each delivery has a package identifier, a distance from the warehouse in kilometers, and a package weight in kilograms. Provide a helper to calculate the battery drain per kilometer, which is one percent plus zero point five percent per kilogram of weight. Provide another helper to calculate the total battery required for a round trip. Provide a third helper to check if a delivery requires more than eighty percent battery. The main function should map all deliveries to calculate their round trip battery, filter out those that exceed eighty percent, sort the feasible deliveries by distance ascending, and map them to their identifiers. Example: a two kilogram package at ten kilometers drains forty percent for a round trip.

title: Ski Resort Snow Report
spec: Write a main function `report(trails)` taking an array of mountain trails. Each trail has a name, a difficulty level, and an array of snow depth measurements in inches over the last week. Provide a helper to find the minimum snow depth for a trail. Provide another helper to calculate the average snow depth over the week. Provide a third helper to check if a trail is open, which requires a minimum depth of twenty inches. The main function should filter for open trails, map them to calculate their average depth, filter out any with an average depth below twenty five inches, sort them by average depth descending, and map them to an array of trail names. Example: a trail with measurements of thirty, thirty two, and thirty four is open with an average of thirty two.

title: Recipe Scaling Assistant
spec: Write a main function `scale(recipes)` taking an array of cooking recipes. Each recipe has a title, a base serving size, and an array of ingredient names. Provide a helper to calculate a scaling factor by dividing a target serving size of twelve by the base serving size. Provide another helper to check if a recipe requires a scaling factor greater than one. Provide a third helper to format a string combining the title and the scaling factor. The main function should map the recipes to include their scaling factor, filter for those needing scaling up, filter out any with a scaling factor greater than four, sort them alphabetically by title, and map them using the formatting helper. Example: a base recipe for six servings yields a scaling factor of two.

title: Theme Park Wait Times
spec: Process a list of amusement park attractions where each contains the ride name, a list of recorded wait times in minutes, and a boolean indicating if it is operating. First, ignore all non-operating rides. For each operating ride, calculate the average wait time. Find the ride with the shortest average wait. Next, check if there is any operating ride with an average wait under 15 minutes. Then, extract the names of all rides that have an average wait exceeding 45 minutes. Finally, calculate the total combined wait time of all operating rides. Return a list containing the shortest ride name, the boolean for a short wait existing, the list of long wait names, and the total combined wait time. Example input: a list with one operating ride named coaster with wait times 10 and 20. Expected output: a list containing coaster, false, an empty list, and 15. Entry function is `evaluate(rides)`.

title: Bakery Inventory Forecaster
spec: Given a list of pastry orders, each containing a pastry name, an order quantity, and a list of required ingredients with their base amounts for one unit, calculate the total shopping list. First, determine the total amount needed for each ingredient by multiplying the base amount by the order quantity for every order. Consolidate these amounts so each ingredient appears only once with its total required weight. Exclude any ingredient where the total required weight is less than 50 grams. Sort the remaining ingredients alphabetically by their name. Check if all orders require flour by verifying every order ingredient list. Return a list containing the sorted ingredient names, the total weight of all remaining ingredients combined, and the boolean result for flour. Example input: one order for 2 cakes requiring base amounts of 100 flour and 20 yeast. Expected output: a list containing flour, 200, and true. Entry function is `forecast(orders)`.

title: Arcade High Score Auditor
spec: Process a list of player records where each contains a player name and a list of numerical scores. First, discard any scores that are not a multiple of 10, as these are mathematically impossible in this arcade game. Discard any player who has no valid scores remaining. For each valid player, find their highest valid score. Calculate the average of these highest scores across all valid players. Check if any player achieved a score exactly equal to 9990. Sort the valid players by their highest score in descending order and extract just their names. Return a list containing the names of the sorted valid players, the average high score, and the boolean check for the specific score. Example input: a player named bob with scores 10, 15, and 20. Expected output: a list containing bob, 20, and false. Entry function is `audit(scores)`.

title: Public Transit Delay Analyzer
spec: Process transit route data where each route contains a route identifier, a list of scheduled travel times, and a list of actual travel times. Calculate the delay for each trip by subtracting the scheduled time from the actual time. Determine the average delay for each route. Filter out routes where the average delay is less than 5 minutes. For the remaining delayed routes, find the route with the maximum average delay. Count the total number of individual trips across all delayed routes that had a delay of exactly 0. Sort the delayed routes by their identifier alphabetically. Return a list containing the identifier of the most delayed route, the count of on time trips, and a list of the sorted delayed route identifiers. Example input: a route named express with scheduled times 10 and 20, and actual times 15 and 30. Expected output: a list containing express, 0, and a list containing express. Entry function is `analyze(routes)`.

title: Community Garden Allocator
spec: Allocate garden plots based on a list of gardener requests where each contains a gardener name, a requested minimum area, and a list of preferred crop types. The available plots are provided as a separate list inside the function, with each plot having an identifier and an area. First, map each gardener to a list of plots that meet their minimum area requirement. If a gardener has no suitable plots, remove them from the list. Determine if every valid gardener requested tomatoes as a preferred crop. Find the gardener who requested the largest minimum area. Calculate the total requested area across all valid gardeners. Return a list containing the name of the gardener needing the most space, the boolean regarding tomatoes, and a list of names of the valid gardeners. Example input: a gardener named sue requesting 10 area and tomatoes, with an internally available plot of area 20. Expected output: a list containing sue, true, and a list containing sue. Entry function is `allocate(requests)`.

title: Solar Panel Output Tracker
spec: Analyze daily energy output for an array of solar panels. Each panel record contains a serial number, a list of daily output readings in watt hours, and a year of installation. First, calculate the total weekly output for each panel by summing its daily readings. Exclude any panel installed before 2010. For the remaining panels, check if there is any panel that produced 0 watt hours on any day. Find the panel with the highest total weekly output. Calculate the average weekly output of these recent panels. Sort the serial numbers of the recent panels by their total output in ascending order. Return a list containing the highest producing serial number, the zero output boolean, the average output, and the sorted list of serial numbers. Example input: a panel serial alpha installed in 2015 with daily readings of 10, 20, and 0. Expected output: a list containing alpha, true, 30, and a list containing alpha. Entry function is `track(panels)`.

title: Art Gallery Auction Bids
spec: Evaluate a list of artworks at an auction. Each artwork record contains an artist name, a reserve price, and a list of submitted bid amounts. For each artwork, filter out any bids that are lower than the reserve price. Determine the highest valid bid for each artwork. If an artwork has no valid bids, its highest bid is 0. Calculate the total expected revenue by summing the highest valid bids of all artworks. Extract a list of artist names whose artworks received no valid bids. Check if all artworks received at least one valid bid. Sort the artworks that sold by their highest bid in descending order, returning just the artist names. Return a list containing the total revenue, the boolean for all selling, the list of unsold artist names, and the list of sold artist names. Example input: an artwork by picasso with a reserve of 50 and bids of 40 and 60. Expected output: a list containing 60, true, an empty list, and a list containing picasso. Entry function is `evaluate(artworks)`.

title: Wildlife Camera Trap Counter
spec: Process data from camera traps where each record contains a camera location name, a list of animal counts per photo, and a primary habitat type. First, calculate the total number of animals seen by each camera by summing the counts. Filter the cameras to keep only those located in a forest habitat. Check if any forest camera recorded a photo with more than 20 animals at once. Determine the average number of animals seen across all forest cameras. Sort the forest cameras by their total animal count in descending order. Extract the location names of the top three busiest forest cameras. Return a list containing the top three location names, the boolean for large groups, and the overall average animal count for forest cameras. Example input: a forest camera at river with counts of 2 and 3. Expected output: a list containing river, false, and 5. Entry function is `process(cameras)`.

title: Recycling Center Sorting
spec: Analyze batches of recycled materials where each batch contains a material name, a total weight, and a list of contamination percentages from random samples. First, calculate the average contamination percentage for each batch. Discard any batch where the average contamination is greater than 15 percent. Calculate the total weight of all remaining clean batches. Check if every clean batch is made of glass. Find the clean batch with the lowest average contamination. Create a list of material names from the clean batches, sorted alphabetically. Return a list containing the lowest contamination material name, the total clean weight, the boolean checking for glass, and the sorted list of clean material names. Example input: a batch of glass weighing 100 with contamination samples of 5 and 15. Expected output: a list containing glass, 100, true, and a list containing glass. Entry function is `sort(batches)`.

title: Theater Seating Optimizer
spec: Optimize theater seating for a list of booking requests. Each request contains a patron name, a requested group size, and a list of acceptable row letters. The theater has a fixed capacity per row defined internally. First, determine if each requested row has enough capacity for the group size. Filter out requests that have no acceptable rows with sufficient capacity. For each valid request, assign them to the acceptable row that appears first alphabetically. Check if any valid request asked for a group size larger than 10. Calculate the total number of seats assigned across all valid requests. Extract the names of the valid patrons sorted by their group size in descending order. Return a list with the total assigned seats, the large group boolean, and the sorted patron names. Example input: patron dan requesting 4 seats in row a, where row a has capacity 10. Expected output: a list containing 4, false, and a list containing dan. Entry function is `optimize(requests)`.

title: Food Truck Route Planner
spec: Plan a route from a list of potential food truck stops. Each stop has a neighborhood name, an estimated foot traffic count, and a list of competitor truck distances. First, exclude any stop where there is a competitor truck less than 2 miles away. For the remaining stops, calculate the expected revenue by multiplying the foot traffic by 5. Filter out stops where the expected revenue is below 500. Check if all valid stops are expected to generate over 1000. Find the stop with the highest expected revenue. Sort the valid stops by revenue in ascending order and extract their neighborhood names. Return a list containing the most profitable neighborhood name, the boolean for high revenue, and the sorted list of valid neighborhood names. Example input: neighborhood downtown with foot traffic 200 and competitor distances of 3 and 4 miles. Expected output: a list containing downtown, true, and a list containing downtown. Entry function is `plan(stops)`.

title: Craft Beer Recipe Adjuster
spec: Adjust ingredients for a list of beer recipes. Each recipe contains a beer name, a target batch volume in gallons, and a list of malt weights in pounds. First, calculate a scaling factor for each recipe by dividing the target volume by 5. Multiply all malt weights in the recipe by this scaling factor. Determine the total scaled malt weight for each recipe. Filter out recipes where the total scaled malt weight exceeds 50 pounds. Check if any remaining recipe requires a specific malt weight under 1 pound. Sort the remaining recipes by their total malt weight in descending order. Extract the names of these valid recipes. Return a list containing the total number of valid recipes, the small addition boolean, and the sorted list of beer names. Example input: a stout recipe for 10 gallons needing 20 pounds of malt. Expected output: a list containing 1, false, and a list containing stout. Entry function is `adjust(recipes)`.

title: Local Produce Box Builder
spec: Build produce boxes from a list of available crops. Each crop has a vegetable name, a total harvested weight, and a list of farm distances in miles. First, calculate the average distance for each crop. Filter out crops where the average distance is greater than 50 miles. For the local crops, divide the total harvested weight by the box count of 20 to find the weight per box. Check if every local crop provides at least 1 pound per box. Find the local crop that provides the highest weight per box. Sort the local crops alphabetically by their vegetable name. Return a list containing the highest providing vegetable name, the boolean for minimum weight, and the sorted list of local vegetable names. Example input: crop carrots with harvested weight of 40 and farm distances of 10 and 20 miles. Expected output: a list containing carrots, true, and a list containing carrots. Entry function is `build(inventory)`.

title: Surf School Lesson Scheduler
spec: Schedule surf lessons from a list of student profiles. Each profile contains a student name, a preferred wave height in feet, and a list of available hours. First, filter out students who prefer wave heights over 6 feet, as they require advanced instructors. For the remaining students, count the number of available hours they have. Remove students who have fewer than 3 available hours. Check if any valid student is available at 8 in the morning. Calculate the total number of available hours across all valid students. Sort the valid students by their available hour count in descending order and extract their names. Return a list containing the total available hours, the morning availability boolean, and the sorted list of student names. Example input: student leo with preferred wave height 4 and available hours 8, 9, and 10. Expected output: a list containing 3, true, and a list containing leo. Entry function is `schedule(students)`.

title: Vintage Clothing Grader
spec: Grade a list of vintage garments where each contains an item description, a base value, and a list of damage deduction percentages. First, calculate the total deduction percentage for each item by summing its damage list. If the total deduction exceeds 100 percent, cap it at 100. Calculate the final value of each item by deducting the total percentage from the base value, for example a base value of 100 with a 10 percent deduction becomes 90. Filter out items whose final value is strictly less than 20. Check if all saleable items have zero deductions. Find the saleable item with the highest final value. Sort the saleable items by their final value in ascending order and extract the descriptions. Return a list containing the most valuable item description, the flawless boolean, and the sorted descriptions. Example input: a jacket with base value 50 and deductions of 10 and 20 percent. Expected output: a list containing jacket, false, and a list containing jacket. Entry function is `grade(garments)`.

title: Hiking Trail Difficulty Scorer
spec: Score a list of hiking trails where each contains a trail name, a total distance in miles, and a list of elevation changes in feet for each mile segment. First, calculate the total elevation gain for each trail by summing only the positive elevation changes. Filter out trails that have a total distance less than 3 miles. Calculate a difficulty score by dividing the total elevation gain by the distance. Check if any long trail has a difficulty score over 500. Find the trail with the highest difficulty score. Sort the long trails by their difficulty score in descending order, extracting just the trail names. Return a list containing the hardest trail name, the extreme difficulty boolean, and the sorted trail names. Example input: a trail named summit with distance of 4 miles and elevation changes of 100 and negative 50. Expected output: a list containing summit, false, and a list containing summit. Entry function is `score(trails)`.

title: Boarding Kennel Meal Planner
spec: Plan meals for a list of dogs at a kennel. Each dog record contains a dog name, a weight in pounds, and a list of activity duration in minutes for the past three days. First, calculate the average daily activity duration for each dog. Calculate the daily food requirement: start with 2 cups, add an amount equal to the dog weight divided by 10, and add half a cup if the average activity duration is strictly greater than 60 minutes. Filter out dogs that require less than 3 cups total. Check if every large eater requires more than 5 cups. Sort the large eaters by their total food requirement in descending order and extract their names. Return a list containing the total food required for all large eaters combined, the heavy eater boolean, and the sorted dog names. Example input: a 40 pound dog named rex with activity durations of 50 and 40. Expected output: a list containing 6, true, and a list containing rex. Entry function is `plan(dogs)`.

title: Indie Game Achievement Tracker
spec: Track achievements from a list of player sessions. Each session contains a player identifier, a list of levels completed, and a list of coins collected per level. First, calculate the total coins collected in each session by summing the coin list. Filter out sessions where the player completed fewer than 5 levels. Check if any valid session collected more than 1000 coins in total. Determine the average number of coins collected across all valid sessions. Find the player identifier that had the highest total coins among valid sessions. Sort the valid player identifiers alphabetically. Return a list containing the highest collecting player identifier, the extreme collector boolean, the average coin count, and the sorted list of valid player identifiers. Example input: player one completing 6 levels and collecting 10 coins each. Expected output: a list containing one, false, 60, and a list containing one. Entry function is `track(players)`.

title: Pottery Kiln Temperature Monitor
spec: Monitor a list of kiln firing logs. Each log contains a firing date, a target peak temperature, and a list of recorded temperatures taken every hour. First, find the maximum recorded temperature for each log. Calculate the shortfall by subtracting the maximum recorded temperature from the target peak temperature. Filter out logs where the shortfall is greater than 50 degrees, considering them failed firings. Check if all successful firings reached a maximum temperature over 2000 degrees. Calculate the average maximum temperature of the successful firings. Sort the successful firings by their firing date chronologically and extract the dates. Return a list containing the average maximum temperature, the high heat boolean, and the sorted list of successful dates. Example input: log for monday with target 2000 and readings of 1900 and 1960. Expected output: a list containing 1960, false, and a list containing monday. Entry function is `monitor(readings)`.

title: Microbrewery Keg Tracker
spec: Process a list of keg rental records. Each record contains a customer name, a keg volume in gallons, and a list of days the keg has been out over multiple rentals. First, calculate the average days out for each customer by averaging their list. Filter out customers whose average days out is greater than 30. Calculate the total volume rented by each valid customer. Check if any valid customer rented a volume of exactly 15 gallons. Find the valid customer with the highest total volume. Sort the valid customers alphabetically by name. Return a list containing the best customer name, the specific volume boolean, the combined total volume of all valid customers, and the sorted list of valid customer names. Example input: customer bar with volume 10 and days out 10 and 20. Expected output: a list containing bar, false, 10, and a list containing bar. Entry function is `manage(kegs)`.

title: Escape Room Puzzle Reset
spec: Generate a reset report for a list of escape rooms. Each room contains a room theme, a base reset time in minutes, and a list of misplaced prop counts from recent games. First, calculate the average number of misplaced props for each room. Calculate the expected reset time by adding the base reset time to the average misplaced prop count multiplied by 2. Filter out rooms where the expected reset time is less than 10 minutes. Check if every complex room has an expected reset time under 30 minutes. Find the room theme with the longest expected reset time. Sort the complex room themes by their expected reset time in ascending order. Return a list containing the longest room theme, the quick reset boolean, and the sorted list of themes. Example input: theme pirate with base reset time 5 and misplaced prop counts of 4 and 6. Expected output: a list containing pirate, true, and a list containing pirate. Entry function is `generate(items)`.

title: Bicycle Fleet Maintenance
spec: Schedule maintenance from a list of rental bicycles. Each bicycle contains a bike code, a months in service count, and a list of miles ridden per month. First, calculate the total miles ridden for each bicycle by summing the monthly miles. Filter out bicycles that have been in service for less than 6 months. Calculate the average miles ridden per month for these older bicycles. Check if any older bicycle has a total mileage exceeding 5000 miles. Find the bike code with the highest total mileage. Sort the older bicycles by their average monthly miles in descending order and extract the bike codes. Return a list containing the highest mileage bike code, the extreme mileage boolean, and the sorted list of older bike codes. Example input: bike code x with 10 months in service and monthly miles of 50 and 100. Expected output: a list containing x, false, and a list containing x. Entry function is `schedule(bicycles)`.

title: Youth Soccer League Standings
spec: Calculate standings from a list of team records. Each team contains a mascot name, a base penalty deduction, and a list of goals scored in each match. First, calculate the total goals scored by each team by summing their match goals. Subtract the base penalty deduction from the total goals to get the final score.
