Filter out teams that have a final score below 0. Check if all valid teams scored at least 1 goal in every match they played. Find the mascot name of the team with the highest final score. Calculate the average final score of the valid teams. Sort the valid teams by final score in descending order and extract the mascot names. Return a list containing the winning mascot name, the consistent scorer boolean, the average score, and the sorted mascot names. Example input: team tigers with deduction 1 and match goals of 2 and 3. Expected output: a list containing tigers, true, 4, and a list containing tigers. Entry function is `calculate(matches)`.

title: Urban Tree Planting Planner
spec: Plan tree planting from a list of proposed street segments. Each segment contains a street name, an available soil volume, and a list of utility pipe depths in inches. First, find the minimum utility pipe depth for each segment. Filter out segments where the minimum pipe depth is less than 24 inches. Calculate a suitability score for the remaining segments by multiplying the soil volume by the minimum pipe depth. Check if any suitable segment has a soil volume over 100. Find the street name with the highest suitability score. Sort the suitable segments alphabetically by street name. Return a list containing the best street name, the large volume boolean, the total suitability score of all valid segments, and the sorted list of valid street names. Example input: street main with soil volume 50 and pipe depths of 30 and 40 inches. Expected output: a list containing main, false, 1500, and a list containing main. Entry function is `plan(locations)`.

title: Amateur Radio Contest Scorer
spec: Score an amateur radio contest from a list of participant logs. Each log contains a callsign, an operator class, and a list of contact distances in kilometers. First, calculate the points for each contact: 1 point for distances under 500, and 3 points for distances 500 or more. Sum these points to get the raw score for each participant. Filter out participants with a raw score of 0. Multiply the raw score by 2 if the operator class is novice. Check if every valid participant made at least one contact over 1000 kilometers. Find the callsign with the highest final score. Sort the valid callsigns by final score in descending order. Return a list containing the winning callsign, the extreme distance boolean, and the sorted list of valid callsigns. Example input: callsign alpha, class expert, and distances of 400 and 600. Expected output: a list containing alpha, false, 4, and a list containing alpha. Entry function is `score(logs)`.

title: Book Club Reading Pace
spec: Write a function `evaluate(readers)` that analyzes reading speeds. The input is a list of dictionaries representing readers, each containing a name, a list of chapter lengths in pages, and a list of reading session durations in minutes. Define small helper functions to sum an array of numbers, to calculate a reader's total pages, and to calculate their total time. First, filter the input list to keep only readers with a total time greater than zero. Transform this filtered list to compute each reader's speed in pages per minute. Filter the speeds to keep only those greater than one page per minute. Sort the remaining speeds from highest to lowest. Finally, return the sorted list of speeds. Wrap the execution in a main function that runs the logic on a few test lists.

title: Used Car Depreciation
spec: Create a function `appraise(cars)` to estimate used vehicle values. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a base price, age in years, mileage, and condition out of ten. Define helper functions to calculate the age penalty (age multiplied by two hundred) and the mileage penalty (mileage multiplied by zero point one). Filter the list to include only cars newer than twenty years. Transform the filtered list to compute the final value for each car, which is the base price minus both penalties, plus a bonus of one hundred for every condition point above five. Filter out any cars with a final value of zero or less. Sort the valid values from highest to lowest. Return the sorted list of values. Include a short main block that tests the function with a couple of example inputs.

title: Aquarium Water Quality
spec: Implement a function `monitor(tanks)` to check water conditions. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a tank identifier, a list of acidity readings, and a list of ammonia levels. Create helper functions to compute the average of a list of numbers, and to check if a tank has any ammonia reading above zero point five. Filter the list of tanks to keep only those that have high ammonia. Transform the remaining tanks into a list of their average acidity readings. Filter these averages to keep only those outside the safe range of six point five to eight. Sort the dangerous acidity levels in ascending order. Return the sorted list. Provide a driver routine that passes multiple scenarios to the function to demonstrate the logic.

title: Holiday Gift Budget Allocation
spec: Develop a function `allocate(friends)` to manage gift budgets. The input is a list of dictionaries, each having a recipient name, a relationship tier from one to three, and a list of item prices from their wish list. Define a helper function to determine the budget limit, which is fifty times the relationship tier. Define another helper to find the most expensive item in a list that is under a given budget. Filter the friends to keep only those with at least one item on their wish list. Transform the list to find the allocated gift price for each friend using the helpers. Filter out the prices that are zero, meaning nothing was affordable. Sort the allocated prices from lowest to highest. Return the sum of these prices. Include a test runner that executes the function on various inputs.

title: Farm Animal Feed Rations
spec: Write a function `ration(animals)` to calculate daily feed requirements. The input is a list of dictionaries, each containing a species, weight in kilograms, age, and an activity multiplier. Create a helper function to calculate the base feed amount, which is weight multiplied by zero point zero five. Create another helper to calculate the total feed by multiplying the base amount by the activity multiplier. Filter the animals to include only those weighing more than ten kilograms. Transform the list to compute the total feed required for each animal. Filter out any feed amounts less than one. Sort the remaining feed amounts in descending order. Return the sorted list of feed requirements. Add a short main block to execute the function on several sample lists.

title: Cloud Server Load Balancer
spec: Implement a function `balance(servers)` to evaluate server loads. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a server identifier, maximum capacity, and a list of active job sizes. Define helper functions to calculate the sum of an array of job sizes and to compute the utilization percentage (total job size divided by maximum capacity, multiplied by one hundred). Filter the servers to keep only those with at least one active job. Transform the filtered list to compute the utilization percentage for each server. Filter the percentages to keep only those above eighty percent, which indicates high load. Sort the high load percentages from highest to lowest. Return the sorted list of percentages. Create a driver block that invokes the function with different data sets.

title: Call Center Wait Times
spec: Write a function `analyze(calls)` to review lengthy support calls. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a hold time in seconds, a talk time in seconds, and a resolution status. Define a helper function to calculate the total duration of a call by adding hold time and talk time. Define another helper to determine if a call was abandoned, meaning it has a hold time over three hundred seconds and is not resolved. Filter out all abandoned calls from the list. Transform the remaining calls into a list of their total durations. Filter this list to keep only durations longer than six hundred seconds. Sort the lengthy durations in descending order. Return the average of these lengthy durations. Include a test section that processes multiple lists of calls.

title: Tailor Measurements Converter
spec: Create a function `convert(clients)` to process clothing measurements. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a client name and a list of measurements in inches. Define a helper function to convert a single measurement from inches to centimeters by multiplying by two point five four. Define another helper to convert an entire list of measurements into their centimeter equivalents and sum them. Filter the list to include only clients who have provided at least three measurements. Transform the list of clients to compute their total measurement sum in centimeters. Filter out any totals that are less than fifty centimeters. Sort the totals in ascending order. Return the sorted list of totals. Wrap the logic in a main block that runs a few examples.

title: Vinyl Record Collection Appraiser
spec: Develop a function `appraise(records)` to estimate the value of a record collection. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with an artist, a condition rating out of ten, a rarity multiplier, and a list of previous sale prices. Create helper functions to calculate the average of a list of sale prices and to compute the current estimated value (average price multiplied by the rarity multiplier, plus the condition rating). Filter the records to keep only those with at least one previous sale. Transform the remaining records into their estimated current values. Filter the values to keep only those greater than fifty. Sort the values from highest to lowest. Return the sorted list of values. Add a test function that runs the appraisal on different collections.

title: Video Game Level Experience
spec: Write a function `calculate(players)` to update player levels based on recent activity. The input is a list of dictionaries, each containing a username, a base level, a list of experience points gained from monsters, and a quest bonus. Define helper functions to calculate the total experience gained from the list of monsters and to determine the new level, adding one level for every one thousand total points including the quest bonus. Filter the players to include only those who gained experience from at least one monster. Transform the list to compute the new level for each player. Filter out players whose new level is less than ten. Sort the resulting levels in descending order. Return the list of levels. Provide a main execution block to test various scenarios.

title: Bridge Toll Collection
spec: Implement a function `tabulate(vehicles)` to calculate daily toll revenue. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a license plate, axle count, weight in tons, and a boolean indicating if they have an electronic pass. Create a helper function to determine the base toll, which is two for two axles and five for anything more. Create another helper to calculate the final toll by adding a weight surcharge (one per ton over ten tons) and applying a fifty percent discount for electronic passes. Filter the list to keep vehicles with an axle count of at least two. Transform the vehicles to compute their final toll amounts. Filter out any tolls that calculate to zero. Sort the tolls from highest to lowest. Return the total sum of all sorted tolls. Include a driver to test the function.

title: Apartment Noise Complaint Filter
spec: Create a function `filter(complaints)` to identify severe noise issues. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a unit number, a decibel level, the hour of the day, and the duration in minutes. Define helper functions to check if the time is during quiet hours (between ten at night and seven in the morning) and to calculate the severity score (decibel level multiplied by duration). Filter the list to keep only complaints that occurred during quiet hours. Transform the list into a list of severity scores for these complaints. Filter the scores to keep only those above five hundred. Sort the scores in descending order. Return the highest severity score from the list. Wrap this in a main routine that runs the function on a few sample inputs.

title: Courier Package Router
spec: Develop a function `route(packages)` to sort priority deliveries. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a tracking number, a numeric destination zone, weight in kilograms, and a delivery priority level. Create a helper function to check if a package is heavy, meaning it weighs more than twenty kilograms. Create another helper to compute a routing score by multiplying the priority level by the destination zone. Filter the packages to exclude any with a priority level of zero. Transform the list into an array of routing scores. Filter the scores to keep only those greater than fifty. Sort the routing scores from highest to lowest. Return the sorted list of scores. Add a test block to run multiple examples.

title: Home Wi-Fi Signal Heatmap
spec: Write a function `evaluate(rooms)` to find areas with poor internet connection. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a room name, distance from the router, number of walls, and a list of signal strength readings. Define helper functions to calculate the average of the signal readings and to compute a penalty score (distance plus five times the number of walls). Filter the rooms to keep only those that have at least one signal reading. Transform the list to compute the final signal score for each room, which is the average reading minus the penalty score. Filter the scores to keep only those below fifty, indicating poor signal. Sort these poor scores in ascending order, from worst to best. Return the sorted list of scores. Include a driver function to test various room lists.

title: Grocery Expiration Sorter
spec: Implement a function `sort(items)` to manage perishable inventory. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with an item name, category, total shelf life in days, and days since it was stocked. Create a helper function to calculate the days remaining before expiration. Create another helper to check if an item is highly perishable, such as those in the dairy or produce categories. Filter the list to exclude items with more than ten days remaining. Transform the list to an array of remaining days for the items. Filter the remaining days to keep only those less than five. Sort the remaining days in ascending order. Return the sorted list. Provide a main block that passes a few test inventories to the function.

title: Paint Mixing Ratio Calculator
spec: Write a function `mix(formulas)` to prepare custom paint orders. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a color name, a list of base pigment amounts in ounces, and a desired final volume in gallons. Define helper functions to sum the base pigments and to calculate a scale factor based on the desired volume. Filter the formulas to keep only those that contain at least two pigments. Transform the list to compute the total ounces of pigment required for each formula after applying the scale factor. Filter the required ounces to keep only amounts less than one hundred. Sort the required amounts in ascending order. Return the list of required amounts. Wrap the function call in a driver routine that tests multiple batches of formulas.

title: Software Bug Triage
spec: Create a function `triage(bugs)` to prioritize development tasks. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a severity level, number of affected users, and a list of developer comments. Define helper functions to compute a priority score (severity multiplied by the number of affected users) and to check if a bug has more than three comments. Filter the list to keep only unresolved bugs, which are those with a severity level above zero. Transform the filtered list to compute the priority score for each bug. Filter the priority scores to keep only those above fifty. Sort the high priority scores from highest to lowest. Return the sum of these sorted scores. Include a small test runner to execute the function on various bug lists.

title: Delivery Truck Payload Balancer
spec: Implement a function `balance(trucks)` to optimize fleet loading. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a truck identifier, maximum weight capacity, and a list of current parcel weights. Create helper functions to sum the parcel weights and to calculate the remaining capacity of a truck. Filter the list of trucks to include only those that have at least one parcel loaded. Transform the list to compute the remaining capacity for each truck. Filter these capacities to keep only those under five hundred, indicating the truck is nearly full. Sort the remaining capacities in ascending order. Return the sorted list of capacities. Add a main execution function that runs the logic on a few different fleet scenarios.

title: Greenhouse Humidity Controller
spec: Develop a function `regulate(zones)` to monitor climate control systems. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a zone identifier, a target humidity percentage, and a list of recent humidity readings. Define helper functions to calculate the average of the recent readings and to find the absolute difference between the average and the target humidity. Filter the list to keep only zones that have recorded at least three readings. Transform the list into an array of the absolute differences for each zone. Filter the differences to keep only those greater than five percent, which require adjustment. Sort the differences from highest to lowest. Return the sorted list of differences. Provide a test section that evaluates multiple greenhouse setups.

title: Fishing Catch Limit Verifier
spec: Write a function `verify(anglers)` to enforce local wildlife regulations. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with an angler name, license status, and a list of fish lengths caught in inches. Create helper functions to determine if a single fish is of legal size (over fifteen inches) and to count how many legal fish are in a list. Filter the anglers to include only those with an active license. Transform the list to compute the count of legal fish caught by each angler. Filter the counts to keep only those greater than five, indicating the angler is over the limit. Sort these counts in descending order. Return the sum of all the over-limit counts. Include a short test block that runs the function.

title: Daily Calorie Burn Target
spec: Implement a function `track(workouts)` to analyze fitness progress. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with an exercise name, duration in minutes, an intensity multiplier, and a list of heart rate readings. Define helper functions to calculate the average heart rate and to estimate the calories burned (duration multiplied by intensity and the average heart rate factor). Filter the list to keep workouts that lasted at least ten minutes. Transform the list to compute the estimated calories burned for each workout. Filter the calories to keep only amounts greater than fifty. Sort the calorie amounts from highest to lowest. Return the total sum of these calorie amounts. Wrap the logic in a driver function that tests various workout lists.

title: Language Translation Progress
spec: Create a function `measure(documents)` to track localization efforts. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a document title, total word count, and a list of word counts for translated segments. Create helper functions to sum the translated segment word counts and to calculate the completion percentage. Filter the documents to keep only those with a total word count greater than zero. Transform the list into an array of completion percentages. Filter the percentages to keep only those less than one hundred, indicating incomplete documents. Sort the incomplete percentages in ascending order. Return the sorted list of percentages. Add a main block that runs the function on a few test lists.

title: Office Desk Reassignment
spec: Develop a function `reassign(employees)` to manage workspace allocations. The input is a list of dictionaries, each containing a department, days in the office per week, and a list of numeric desk zone preferences. Define helper functions to check if an employee is full-time in the office (more than three days) and to extract their top preferred desk zone, which is the first number in their preference list. Filter the employees to keep only those in the engineering department. Transform the list into an array of their top preferred desk zones. Filter the zones to keep only those with a zone number greater than zero. Sort the zone numbers in ascending order. Return the sorted list. Provide a test runner to execute the logic on multiple inputs.

title: City Bus Route Efficiency
spec: Write a function `evaluate(routes)` to analyze public transit performance. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a route identifier, total distance, and a list of passenger counts at various stops. Create helper functions to sum the passenger counts and to calculate the efficiency score (total passengers divided by total distance). Filter the routes to keep only those that have at least five stops recorded. Transform the list into an array of efficiency scores. Filter the scores to keep only those less than two, which indicate underperforming routes. Sort the underperforming scores in ascending order. Return the average of these scores. Include a driver routine to test the function with different route lists.

title: Mountain Bike Trail Condition
spec: Create a function `assess(trails)` to review park safety. The input is a list of dictionaries, each with a trail name, a base difficulty rating, and a list of recent obstacle severity reports ranging from one to ten. Define helper functions to count the number of high severity obstacles (those rated over seven) and to compute an adjusted difficulty score by adding the high severity count to the base rating. Filter the list to keep only trails that have received at least one obstacle report. Transform the list into an array of adjusted difficulty scores. Filter the scores to keep only those greater than ten. Sort the scores from highest to lowest. Return the sorted list of scores. Wrap the execution in a main function that runs a few sample lists.

title: Avalanche Risk Evaluator
spec:
Implement `evaluate(slopes)` to process a list of mountain slope records. Each slope object contains a name, incline, depth, and fresh value. Discard slopes with an incline under thirty degrees. For the remaining slopes, calculate the total snow as the depth plus the fresh amount. A slope is considered high risk if the total snow is over one hundred and the fresh amount is over twenty. Sort the high risk slopes by incline in descending order. Return an array containing two elements: a list of the high risk slope names, and a list of all unique fresh amounts among all slopes that have an incline of at least thirty degrees.
Example input: [{name: "Alpha", incline: 35, depth: 90, fresh: 25}, {name: "Beta", incline: 20, depth: 50, fresh: 10}]
Example output: [["Alpha"], [25]]

title: Coffee Roasting Optimizer
spec:
Create `optimize(batches)` to analyze coffee roasting data. Each batch object features an origin, target, current, and time value. First, discard any batches where the current temperature is already equal to or greater than the target. Calculate the heating rate for each remaining batch by dividing the current temperature by the time in the roaster. Identify batches that are heating too slowly, defined as a rate below five. From those slow batches, select the ones needing more than fifty degrees to reach their target. Sort these selected batches by origin alphabetically. Return an array containing the origins of these slow batches, followed by a list of all unique target temperatures among all initially retained unfinished batches.
Example input: [{origin: "Brazil", target: 200, current: 150, time: 40}, {origin: "Kenya", target: 200, current: 200, time: 30}]
Example output: [["Brazil"], [200]]

title: Poetry Contest Evaluator
spec:
Write `evaluate(poems)` to review poetry submissions. Each poem object has a title, words, lines, and a rhymes list. Reject poems with fewer than ten lines or more than fifty words. For the valid poems, calculate a rhyme score by dividing the number of elements in the rhymes list by the lines count. A poem is a finalist if its rhyme score is greater than zero point five. Sort the finalists by their words count in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of the finalist titles, and a list of all unique line counts across all valid poems.
Example input: [{title: "Ode", words: 40, lines: 12, rhymes: ["cat", "hat", "mat", "bat", "rat", "fat", "sat"]}]
Example output: [["Ode"], [12]]

title: Historical Artifact Sorter
spec:
Implement `sort(artifacts)` to categorize museum pieces. Each artifact object includes an identifier, era, value, and condition rating out of ten. Ignore artifacts with a condition rating below four. Convert the estimated value to a standardized metric by multiplying the value by the condition rating. Filter for artifacts from the Bronze era that have a standardized metric above five thousand. Sort the resulting artifacts by condition rating in descending order, breaking ties by identifier alphabetically. Return an array containing a list of identifiers for the qualifying artifacts, along with a list of all unique eras among evaluated artifacts that passed the initial condition filter.
Example input: [{identifier: "Vase", era: "Bronze", value: 2000, condition: 5}]
Example output: [["Vase"], ["Bronze"]]

title: Spaceship Trajectory Adjuster
spec:
Create `adjust(maneuvers)` to process orbital corrections. Each maneuver object provides a thruster, fuel, velocity, and a critical boolean flag. Keep only the maneuvers where the velocity change is greater than zero. Calculate efficiency for each by dividing the velocity change by the fuel required. Identify maneuvers that are either marked critical or have an efficiency above two. Sort these selected maneuvers by fuel required in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of the thruster names for the selected maneuvers, and a list of unique velocity changes for all critical maneuvers.
Example input: [{thruster: "Main", fuel: 10, velocity: 25, critical: true}]
Example output: [["Main"], [25]]

title: Bridge Integrity Monitor
spec:
Write `monitor(sensors)` to analyze structural health data. Each sensor object contains a location, amplitude, frequency, and an active boolean status. Process only the sensors that are currently active. Calculate a stress factor by multiplying the vibration amplitude by the frequency. Flag any sensor where the stress factor exceeds one hundred. Sort the flagged sensors by amplitude in descending order. Return an array containing a list of the flagged sensor locations, and a list of unique frequencies among all active sensors.
Example input: [{location: "Arch", amplitude: 5, frequency: 25, active: true}]
Example output: [["Arch"], [25]]

title: Photography Contest Filter
spec:
Implement `filter(entries)` to judge photo submissions. Each entry object includes a photographer, iso, aperture, shutter, and a raw boolean flag. Keep only entries where the raw flag is true. Calculate the exposure value as the iso setting divided by the shutter speed. Reject entries where the exposure value is below one hundred or the aperture is above eight. Sort the remaining entries by iso setting in ascending order. Return an array containing the photographer names of the finalists, followed by a list of all unique aperture values used among the valid raw entries.
Example input: [{photographer: "Alice", iso: 400, aperture: 4, shutter: 2, raw: true}]
Example output: [["Alice"], [4]]

title: Coral Reef Health Assessor
spec:
Create `assess(surveys)` to evaluate oceanographic data. Each survey object has a zone, coverage, bleaching, and temperature value. Discard surveys where the water temperature is below twenty degrees. Calculate a health index as the coral coverage percentage minus twice the bleaching percentage. Identify critical zones where the health index is below thirty. Sort these critical zones by water temperature in descending order. Return an array containing the zone names of critical areas, and a list of unique temperatures across all surveys that met the initial temperature threshold.
Example input: [{zone: "North", coverage: 60, bleaching: 20, temperature: 25}]
Example output: [["North"], [25]]

title: Meteorite Landing Tracker
spec:
Write `track(impacts)` to process asteroid strike data. Each impact object includes a region, mass, velocity, and crater diameter. Keep impacts with a mass greater than fifty. Calculate the kinetic energy equivalent by multiplying the mass by the square of the velocity. Filter out impacts with a kinetic energy less than ten thousand. Sort the remaining significant impacts by crater diameter in descending order. Return an array containing a list of the region strings for these impacts, followed by a list of unique masses observed among the initially filtered impacts.
Example input: [{region: "Desert", mass: 100, velocity: 15, crater: 20}]
Example output: [["Desert"], [100]]

title: Emergency Room Triage Prioritizer
spec:
Implement `prioritize(patients)` to sort hospital admissions. Each patient object provides a name, age, pain, and heart rate. Ignore patients who are under eighteen years old. Calculate a severity score by adding the pain level to the absolute difference between the heart rate and eighty. Select patients with a severity score of twenty or higher. Sort them by age in descending order, then by pain level descending. Return an array containing a list of selected patient names, and a list of unique ages among all adult patients.
Example input: [{name: "John", age: 45, pain: 8, heart: 95}]
Example output: [["John"], [45]]

title: Lighthouse Maintenance Scheduler
spec:
Create `schedule(lighthouses)` to plan coastal inspections. Each lighthouse object has a name, intensity, battery, and days since last check. Process only lighthouses where days is greater than thirty. Calculate a priority metric by dividing the days by the battery level. Identify urgent locations where the bulb intensity is below eighty or the priority metric is above five. Sort the urgent lighthouses by priority metric in descending order. Return an array containing a list of the structure names needing urgent care, and a list of unique battery levels among all processed lighthouses.
Example input: [{name: "Point", intensity: 75, battery: 10, days: 60}]
Example output: [["Point"], [10]]

title: Honeybee Hive Population Estimator
spec:
Write `estimate(hives)` to analyze apiary health. Each hive object contains an identifier, comb, activity, and queen age in months. Discard hives where the queen age is over twenty four months. Calculate the estimated population by multiplying the comb count by the activity rate and then by one hundred. Select hives where the estimated population is less than five thousand. Sort these vulnerable hives by comb count in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of their hive identifiers, along with a list of unique activity rates of all considered hives with young queens.
Example input: [{identifier: "A1", comb: 10, activity: 4, queen: 12}]
Example output: [["A1"], [4]]

title: Passport Visa Validator
spec:
Implement `validate(visas)` to verify travel documents. Each visa object provides a country, duration, issue year, and a multiple boolean flag. Ignore visas where the issue year is before two thousand and fifteen. Calculate a validity score by multiplying the duration by two if the multiple flag is true, or by one otherwise. Keep visas with a validity score of at least ninety. Sort them by issue year in ascending order, breaking ties by duration descending. Return an array containing a list of country codes for the valid visas, and a list of unique issue years for all originally considered visas.
Example input: [{country: "FR", duration: 60, issue: 2018, multiple: true}]
Example output: [["FR"], [2018]]

title: Fencing Tournament Grader
spec:
Create `grade(bouts)` to evaluate competition results. Each bout object includes a fencer, scored, received, and penalty cards count. Keep bouts where the penalty cards are fewer than three. Calculate the touch indicator as the scored touches minus the received touches. Filter fencers whose touch indicator is positive and who scored at least ten touches. Sort the successful fencers by touch indicator in descending order, then by scored touches descending. Return an array containing a list of these fencer names, and a list of unique penalty card counts across all bouts with acceptable penalty levels.
Example input: [{fencer: "Leo", scored: 15, received: 10, penalty: 1}]
Example output: [["Leo"], [1]]

title: Recycling Material Sorter
spec:
Write `sort(materials)` to process waste management data. Each batch object has an id, material, weight, and contamination percentage. Process only batches where the contamination is below fifteen. Calculate the net usable weight by subtracting the contamination percentage of the total weight from the weight itself. Select batches where the net usable weight is over fifty. Sort them by contamination percentage in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of the batch ids, and a list of unique material strings present in the clean batches.
Example input: [{id: "B1", material: "Glass", weight: 100, contamination: 10}]
Example output: [["B1"], ["Glass"]]

title: Glacier Melt Rate Estimator
spec:
Implement `estimate(glaciers)` to assess climate change impacts. Each glacier object contains a name, surface, temperature, and summer days. Exclude glaciers with a temperature below zero. Calculate the annual melt volume by multiplying the surface area by the temperature and then by the summer days. Identify rapidly melting glaciers where the melt volume exceeds ten thousand. Sort them by surface area in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of names of the rapidly melting glaciers, and a list of unique temperature readings for all glaciers initially considered.
Example input: [{name: "Ice", surface: 10, temperature: 2, summer: 600}]
Example output: [["Ice"], [2]]

title: Figure Skating Jump Scorer
spec:
Create `score(jumps)` to tabulate competition marks. Each jump object provides a skater, base, execution, and a fall boolean flag. Keep jumps where the fall flag is false. Calculate the final score by adding the execution grade to the base value. Select jumps where the final score is greater than eight. Sort these excellent jumps by final score in descending order, breaking ties by base value descending. Return an array containing a list of the skater names, and a list of unique base values awarded among all non-falling jumps.
Example input: [{skater: "Anna", base: 6.5, execution: 2.0, fall: false}]
Example output: [["Anna"], [6.5]]

title: Seismograph Tremor Log Processor
spec:
Write `process(tremors)` to analyze earthquake data. Each tremor object includes a station, magnitude, depth, and duration. Discard tremors with a depth greater than fifty. Calculate an impact factor by multiplying the magnitude by the duration. Keep tremors with a magnitude of at least four point zero and an impact factor over twenty. Sort the significant tremors by magnitude in descending order. Return an array containing a list of station strings for these tremors, and a list of unique depths for all valid tremors.
Example input: [{station: "S1", magnitude: 4.5, depth: 10, duration: 10}]
Example output: [["S1"], [10]]

title: Wild Mushroom Foraging Assessor
spec:
Implement `assess(mushrooms)` to grade harvested fungi. Each mushroom object has a species, diameter, stem, and a discoloration boolean flag. Ignore mushrooms that have the discoloration flag set to true. Calculate a volume estimate by multiplying the diameter by the stem length. Select mushrooms where the volume estimate is between twenty and one hundred. Sort the selected mushrooms by diameter in descending order. Return an array containing a list of species names, and a list of unique stem lengths of all clean mushrooms.
Example input: [{species: "Porcini", diameter: 5, stem: 8, discoloration: false}]
Example output: [["Porcini"], [8]]

title: Racecar Pit Stop Analyzer
spec:
Create `analyze(stops)` to evaluate motorsport telemetry. Each stop object provides a driver, tire, fueling, and penalty value. Process stops where the penalty is less than five. Calculate the total stationary time by adding the tire change time, fueling time, and penalty. Identify efficient stops where the stationary time is under fifteen. Sort these efficient stops by tire change time in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of driver names for the efficient stops, and a list of unique penalties across all processed stops.
Example input: [{driver: "Max", tire: 2.5, fueling: 10, penalty: 0}]
Example output: [["Max"], [0]]

title: Kite Flying Contest Ranker
spec:
Write `rank(kites)` to score outdoor aerial events. Each flight object includes a contestant, string, altitude, and wind speed. Exclude flights where the wind speed was above twenty. Calculate a tension index by dividing the string length by the altitude. Keep flights where the altitude is over fifty and the tension index is below two. Sort the qualifying flights by altitude in descending order. Return an array containing a list of contestant names, and a list of unique wind speeds recorded during all safe flights.
Example input: [{contestant: "Tim", string: 100, altitude: 60, wind: 15}]
Example output: [["Tim"], [15]]

title: Planetarium Show Scheduler
spec:
Implement `schedule(shows)` to organize science center programs. Each show object contains a topic, duration, age, and booked seats. Keep shows with a target age of ten or older. Calculate a popularity ratio by dividing the booked seats by the duration. Select shows with a popularity ratio above one point five. Sort them by booked seats in descending order, then by duration ascending. Return an array containing a list of topic strings for the selected shows, and a list of unique ages targeted by all shows aimed at older audiences.
Example input: [{topic: "Mars", duration: 40, age: 12, booked: 80}]
Example output: [["Mars"], [12]]

title: Casino Blackjack Dealer Auditor
spec:
Create `audit(hands)` to verify table game procedures. Each hand object has a dealer, total, cards, and a bust boolean flag. Process only hands where the bust flag is false. Calculate an efficiency score by dividing the card total by the number of cards. Identify hands where the card total is seventeen or higher and the efficiency score is above five. Sort these hands by card total in descending order, then by the number of cards ascending. Return an array containing a list of dealer names, and a list of unique card counts of all non-busting hands.
Example input: [{dealer: "Sam", total: 18, cards: 3, bust: false}]
Example output: [["Sam"], [3]]

title: Submarine Sonar Ping Filter
spec:
Write `filter(pings)` to analyze underwater acoustics. Each ping object includes a sector, time, frequency, and a biological boolean flag. Ignore pings where the biological flag is true. Calculate the distance by multiplying the return time by seven hundred and fifty. Keep pings where the frequency is above ten thousand and the distance is less than five thousand. Sort the remaining pings by return time in ascending order. Return an array containing a list of sector strings, and a list of unique return times observed among all non-biological pings.
Example input: [{sector: "Alpha", time: 4, frequency: 12000, biological: false}]
Example output: [["Alpha"], [4]]

title: Butterfly Conservatory Inventory
spec:
Implement `manage(butterflies)` to track insect populations. Each butterfly object provides a species, wingspan, days, and an active boolean flag. Discard butterflies where the active flag is false. Calculate a development index by dividing the wingspan by the days spent in pupa. Select butterflies with a wingspan over five and a development index greater than zero point five. Sort them by wingspan in descending order. Return an array containing a list of species names for the selected butterflies, and a list of unique wingspans among all active butterflies.
Example input: [{species: "Monarch", wingspan: 10, days: 14, active: true}]
Example output: [["Monarch"], [10]]

title: Sailing Regatta Scorer
spec: Write a function `score(results)` to process regatta data. Boats have a name and an array of race placements. Define helpers to find the highest placement value, calculate the net score by summing all placements and subtracting the highest one, and format the output. Filter out boats that did not finish all five races. Sort the remaining boats by their net score ascending. Return an array of the sorted boat names. Example input: name Alpha, placements two, one, four, one, five. Example output: Alpha.

title: Trampoline Gymnastics Qualifier
spec: Implement `rank(routines)` for a gymnastics event. Routines have an athlete name, an array of five execution scores, and a single difficulty score. Define helpers to drop the highest and lowest execution scores, sum the remaining three, calculate the final score by adding the difficulty score, and check qualification. Filter out routines with a final score below fifty. Return a list of athlete names sorted by final score descending. Example input: name Jane, execution eight, nine, eight, seven, nine, difficulty fourteen. Example output: Jane.

title: Bird Migration Tracker
spec: Create `analyze(sightings)` for bird watching logs. Sightings have a species name, a flock size, and a latitude coordinate. Define separate helpers to check if a species is the target species to ignore, extract the flock sizes, and calculate the mathematical average. Filter out sightings of the ignored species. Calculate the average flock size for the remaining sightings. Find the maximum latitude reached among them. Return a sentence stating the average size and maximum latitude. Example input: species Robin, size ten, latitude forty. Example output: Average size ten, max latitude forty.

title: Hackathon Project Evaluator
spec: Design `evaluate(projects)` to score submissions. Projects have a title, an array of four component scores, and a boolean indicating late submission. Define distinct helper steps to average the component scores, deduct ten points if the late boolean is true, and check if the final score is passing. Filter out projects that score below sixty. Sort the remaining projects descending by score. Return a list of project titles. Example input: title App, scores eighty, ninety, eighty, ninety, late false. Example output: App.

title: Archery Target Scorer
spec: Develop `tally(archers)` to calculate tournament results. Archers have a name and an array of arrow coordinates with horizontal and vertical values. Define separate logic helpers to calculate the distance from the center for each arrow, convert the distance to points where under two is ten points and under five is five points, and sum the points. Return a list of archer names who scored more than twenty points. Example input: name Bob, coordinates horizontal zero, vertical one. Example output: Bob.

title: Scuba Dive Log Analyzer
spec: Write `process(dives)` for a dive shop. Dives have a site name, a depth in meters, and a duration in minutes. Define separate helpers for checking if the depth is greater than twenty meters, converting durations from minutes to hours, and extracting the site names. Filter for dives deeper than twenty meters. Sum the total hours of these deep dives. Return an array containing the total hours and the list of site names. Example input: site Reef, depth thirty, duration sixty. Example output: one, Reef.

title: Robot Maze Path Evaluator
spec: Implement `navigate(paths)` to evaluate pathfinding algorithms. Paths have a robot identifier and an array of directional commands such as up, down, left, right. Define helpers for updating coordinates starting from zero zero based on the command, calculating the total distance traveled by counting commands, and checking if the final coordinates match five five. Filter robots that end up exactly at the target. Sort them by shortest distance traveled. Return the names of the successful robots. Example input: identifier Bot, commands up, up, right, right. Example output: empty array.

title: Go Kart Lap Time Analyzer
spec: Create `analyze(racers)` to process karting laps. Racers have a name and an array of lap times in seconds. Create helpers for filtering out invalid laps that took longer than sixty seconds, finding the minimum lap time, and calculating the average of valid laps. For each racer, keep only valid laps, find their fastest lap, and calculate their average. Sort racers by their fastest lap ascending. Return their names. Example input: name Speed, laps fifty, fifty five, sixty five. Example output: Speed.

title: Sommelier Wine Tasting Ranker
spec: Design `rank(wines)` to filter blind tasting scores. Wines have a label, a region, and scores for aroma, taste, and finish. Use helpers for region checking, summing the three score criteria, and qualification checking. Filter out wines from a specific excluded region. Calculate the total score for each wine. Filter wines that have a total score of at least eighty. Sort the remaining wines descending by score. Return the wine labels. Example input: label Red, region West, aroma thirty, taste thirty, finish thirty. Example output: Red.

title: Debate Tournament Speaker Points
spec: Develop `evaluate(speakers)` to award debate points. Speakers have a name, a boolean for novice status, and an array of five judge scores. Separate the steps into helpers for finding and removing the highest and lowest scores, averaging the middle three scores, and adding a half point bonus if they are a novice. Filter speakers with an average above twenty seven. Sort them descending. Return the speaker names. Example input: name Alex, novice true, scores twenty eight, twenty eight, twenty eight, twenty eight, twenty eight. Example output: Alex.

title: Orienteering Race Checkpoints
spec: Write `score(runners)` to track an outdoor race. Runners have a name and an array of checkpoint times in minutes. Define helpers for calculating the time differences between consecutive checkpoints, finding the maximum time difference which represents the longest single leg, and summing the total time. Filter runners whose total time is under one hundred minutes. Return a list of sentences describing the runner name and their longest leg. Example input: name Sam, times ten, twenty, thirty five. Example output: Sam longest leg fifteen.

title: Baking Competition Judging
spec: Implement `judge(bakers)` for a pastry show. Bakers have a name, a boolean for time limit exceeded, and scores for presentation, taste, and texture. Implement separate helpers for multiplying taste by two, summing presentation, the doubled taste, and texture, and deducting five points if they exceeded the time limit. Filter bakers scoring over forty points. Sort them by final score descending. Return the baker names. Example input: name Dan, exceeded false, presentation ten, taste ten, texture ten. Example output: Dan.

title: Table Tennis League Rankings
spec: Create `standings(players)` to determine the winner of a ping pong league. Players have a name and an array of match results, each containing games won and games lost. Write helpers for aggregating total games won, aggregating total games lost, and calculating the win ratio of won divided by total games. Filter out players who played fewer than ten total games. Sort descending by win ratio. Return the player names. Example input: name Eve, matches won three, lost one. Example output: empty array.

title: Chess Tournament Tiebreaker
spec: Design `tiebreak(players)` to resolve tournament ties. Players have a name, their own tournament score, and an array of their opponents scores. Use helpers for summing the opponent scores to calculate a tiebreaker value, filtering players who have a tournament score of at least five, and performing a sort comparison. Sort the qualified players first by their tournament score descending, then by their tiebreaker score descending. Return the player names. Example input: name Max, score six, opponents four, five, six. Example output: Max.

title: Film Festival Submission Filter
spec: Develop `screen(films)` to find valid short films. Films have a title, a duration in minutes, and an array of genre tags. Create helpers for checking if the duration is strictly between ten and thirty minutes, checking if the tags include a specific target genre, and extracting the titles. Keep only films that match both duration and genre criteria. Extract the titles of the qualifying films and sort them alphabetically. Return the titles. Example input: title Drama, duration twenty, tags art, indie. Example output: empty array.

title: Synchronized Swimming Scorer
spec: Write `score(routines)` for a pool event. Routines have a team name, an array of technical scores, an array of artistic scores, and a boolean for synchronization errors. Implement separate helpers for dropping the minimum score from an array, averaging an array, and combining the final totals. Sum the technical average and artistic average. Deduct two points if there was an error. Rank teams by their final score descending. Return the team names. Example input: name Aqua, technical eight, nine, artistic eight, nine, error false. Example output: Aqua.

title: Language School Class Placement
spec: Implement `place(students)` to organize learners. Students have a name and an array of grammar and vocabulary test scores. Use helpers for summing the scores, averaging them, and assigning a level based on thresholds. Calculate the overall average score for each student. Assign them to advanced if the average is above eighty, intermediate if above fifty, and beginner otherwise. Group the student names by their assigned level. Return an array containing the advanced students followed by the intermediate students. Example input: name Leo, scores ninety, ninety. Example output: Leo.

title: Drone Racing Obstacle Penalties
spec: Create `process(pilots)` to evaluate drone flights. Pilots have a name, a base course time, and an array of missed obstacles. Separate helpers should be used for penalty calculation by adding five seconds for each missed obstacle, summing the final time, and formatting the output strings. Filter out pilots whose total time exceeds one hundred seconds. Sort the remaining pilots by total time ascending. Return a list of sentences stating the pilot name and total time. Example input: name Mia, base fifty, missed gate one. Example output: Mia time fifty five.

title: Rock Climbing Route Grades
spec: Design `assess(climbers)` for a climbing gym. Climbers have a name and an array of numerical route difficulties they completed. Write helpers for filtering out any difficulties below five, finding the maximum value in an array, and averaging an array of numbers. Find the hardest route completed by each climber. Calculate the average difficulty of their valid routes. Sort climbers by their hardest route descending. Return the climber names. Example input: name Tom, routes four, six, eight. Example output: Tom.

title: Bowling League Handicap
spec: Develop `calculate(bowlers)` for a bowling alley. Bowlers have a name, a historical average, and an array of scores for three recent games. Define helpers for calculating the handicap as eighty percent of two hundred minus the historical average with a minimum of zero, adding the handicap to each recent game, and averaging the adjusted games. Return a list of bowler names whose adjusted average is over one hundred eighty. Example input: name Ron, historical one hundred fifty, games one hundred fifty, one hundred sixty, one hundred seventy. Example output: Ron.

title: Escape Room Puzzle Statistics
spec: Write `analyze(teams)` for an entertainment center. Teams have a name, a boolean for completion status, and an array of times for different puzzles. Create helpers for checking the completion status, summing the puzzle times to get the total time, and finding the maximum puzzle time. Filter for teams that successfully completed the room. Return the names of teams whose total time is under forty five minutes, sorted by their total time ascending. Example input: name Alpha, completion true, times ten, ten, ten. Example output: Alpha.

title: Spelling Bee Advancement
spec: Implement `qualify(contestants)` to advance spellers. Contestants have a name and an array of words they spelled correctly. Use helpers for mapping words to their lengths, summing these lengths to get a total score, and checking the threshold. Calculate the length of each correctly spelled word. Sum these lengths to get a total score. Filter out contestants with a total score below twenty. Sort the remaining contestants descending by score. Return the contestant names. Example input: name Zoe, words dictionary, competition. Example output: Zoe.

title: Marathon Relay Pacing
spec: Create `evaluate(teams)` for a running relay. Teams have a team name and an array of leg times in minutes for four runners. Implement separate helpers for summing the leg times to find the total time, filtering teams whose total time is less than two hundred minutes, and finding the minimum leg time in an array. For qualifying teams, find their fastest single leg time. Return a list of sentences with the team name and fastest leg. Example input: name Fast, times forty, forty, forty, forty. Example output: Fast fastest leg forty.

title: Juggling Competition Analyzer
spec: Design `screen(jugglers)` for a circus talent show. Jugglers have a name and an array of catch sequences, representing consecutive catches without drops. Write helpers for discarding any sequences shorter than ten catches, counting how many times they reached fifty catches, and summing the valid sequence lengths. Keep jugglers who have at least one sequence of fifty and a sum of valid catches greater than two hundred. Return their names sorted alphabetically. Example input: name Jay, sequences fifty, fifty, fifty, fifty, fifty. Example output: Jay.

title: Dog Agility Course Tracker
spec: Develop `score(dogs)` for a pet competition. Dogs have a name, a base run time, and an array of fault codes. Define helpers to count the total number of faults, calculate the final time by adding a three second penalty for each fault and deducting five seconds if faults are zero, and check qualification limits. Filter out dogs whose final time is over sixty seconds. Return the dog names sorted by final time ascending. Example input: name Rex, base fifty, faults jump, tunnel. Example output: Rex.

title: Ice Core Sample Analyzer
spec: Write a function `evaluate(cores)` that processes an array of ice core records. Each record has a year, a depth, a carbon level, and a list of temperature anomalies. First, discard records where the depth is under ten. Next, transform the remaining records into summaries containing the year, the average temperature anomaly calculated from its list, and a carbon risk score which is the carbon level multiplied by the depth. Sort these summaries by the average anomaly in descending order. Find the year of the first summary whose carbon risk score exceeds five thousand, and check if every summary has a positive average anomaly. Finally, extract all temperature anomalies from the valid records into a flat sequence, filter for anomalies strictly greater than zero, and sum them. Return an array containing the year of the highest average anomaly, the year of the found high-risk summary, the boolean from the positive check, and the sum of all positive anomalies. Example input: one record with year two thousand, depth twenty, carbon three hundred, and anomalies two and four. Expected output: a four-element array like [two thousand, two thousand, true, six].

title: Meteorological Balloon Data
spec: Implement `process(balloons)` to analyze weather balloon flights. Each object contains a flight identifier, a launch altitude, and a list of pressure readings. Filter out balloons with a launch altitude below zero. Transform each valid balloon into a summary with its flight identifier and the maximum pressure reading found in its list. Sort the summaries by maximum pressure in descending order. Find the flight identifier of the first summary exceeding one hundred pressure. Check if some summaries have a maximum pressure below fifty. Then, gather all pressure readings from valid balloons into a single list, filter it to keep only readings above twenty, and calculate the sum of these remaining readings. Return an array containing the top flight identifier, the found identifier, the boolean from the check, and the total sum. Example input: a balloon with identifier Alpha, altitude ten, and readings thirty and forty. Output: ['Alpha', undefined, true, seventy].

title: Microbiology Petri Dish Growth
spec: Create a function `evaluate(dishes)` to track bacterial growth. Each dish object has a sample name, an initial cell count, and a list of daily growth percentages. Discard dishes with an initial cell count of zero. Map each remaining dish to an object containing the sample name and the final cell count, which is calculated by applying each daily growth percentage sequentially to the initial count. Sort the results alphabetically by sample name. Find the sample name of the first dish whose final cell count exceeds one million, and check if all valid dishes reached a final count greater than their initial count. Extract a flat list of all daily growth percentages from the valid dishes, filter for percentages greater than ten, and calculate the average of these high percentages. Return an array with the first sorted sample name, the found sample name, the boolean check result, and the average high percentage.

title: Wind Turbine Blade Fatigue
spec: Design a function `inspect(turbines)` to evaluate wind turbine stress. Each input object has a model name, an installation year, and a list of stress test scores. Filter out turbines installed before the year two thousand. Transform each to a summary with the model name and the average stress score. Sort the summaries by average stress score in ascending order. Find the model name of the first summary with an average score below fifty, and check if some summaries have an average score exactly equal to one hundred. Flatten all stress test scores from the valid turbines into a single sequence, filter the sequence for scores above ninety, and sum those critical scores. Return an array containing the lowest stress model name, the found model name, the boolean result, and the sum of critical scores. Example: for a valid turbine model X with scores ninety five and eighty five, the average is ninety, and the critical sum is ninety five.

title: Urban Pothole Repair Prioritizer
spec: Develop `prioritize(reports)` to rank street repairs. Each report object includes a street name, traffic volume, and a list of depth measurements. Discard reports where traffic volume is under five hundred. Map each report to a summary containing the street name and a severity index, calculated as the traffic volume multiplied by the maximum depth measurement in its list. Sort the summaries by severity index in descending order. Find the street name of the first summary with a severity index over ten thousand. Check if every summary has a severity index above one thousand. Combine all depth measurements from the valid reports into one flat list, filter out depths less than five, and sum these deep measurements. Return an array containing the highest severity street name, the found street name, the boolean check, and the sum of deep measurements.

title: Geological Stratigraphy Mapper
spec: Write `map(layers)` to analyze rock formations. Each layer object has a rock type, a base depth, and a list of mineral concentration percentages. Filter out layers with a base depth less than zero. Transform them into summaries containing the rock type and the total mineral concentration obtained by summing the percentages. Sort the summaries by total concentration in descending order. Find the rock type of the first layer with a total concentration over fifty, and check if some layers have a total concentration of exactly zero. Extract all mineral concentration percentages from valid layers into a flat list, filter for percentages greater than five, and multiply all these significant percentages together to form a composite index. Return an array with the top rock type, the found rock type, the boolean result, and the composite index.

title: Deep Sea Vent Temperature Logger
spec: Create `analyze(vents)` to process hydrothermal vent data. Each vent object features a vent zone, depth in meters, and a list of hourly temperature readings. Discard vents shallower than one thousand meters. Map the remaining vents to summaries with the vent zone and the average temperature for that vent. Sort the summaries by average temperature descending. Find the vent zone of the first summary whose average temperature exceeds three hundred degrees, and verify if all summaries have an average temperature above zero. Gather all hourly temperature readings from valid vents into a single flat collection, filter out readings below one hundred degrees, and sum the remaining extreme readings. Return an array containing the hottest vent zone, the found vent zone, the verification boolean, and the sum of extreme readings.

title: Radio Telescope Signal Interference
spec: Implement `filter(signals)` to clean astronomical data. Each signal object has a galaxy source, an antenna baseline, and a list of signal to noise ratios. Filter out signals where the antenna baseline is less than fifty. Transform each to an object containing the galaxy source and the peak ratio, found by determining the maximum value in its list of ratios. Sort the objects by peak ratio in ascending order. Find the galaxy source of the first object with a peak ratio below two. Check if some objects have a peak ratio exactly equal to ten. Extract a flat list of all signal to noise ratios from the valid signals, filter the list to keep ratios between three and seven inclusive, and calculate the average of these mid-range ratios. Return an array with the lowest peak galaxy source, the found galaxy source, the boolean result, and the average mid-range ratio.

title: Aquaponics System Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(tanks)` to manage fish tanks. Each tank object includes a tank identifier, a water volume, and a list of ammonia readings. Discard tanks with a water volume under one hundred liters. Map the remaining tanks to summaries containing the tank identifier and the sum of the ammonia readings. Sort the summaries by the ammonia sum in descending order. Find the tank identifier of the first summary with an ammonia sum over five, and check if every summary has an ammonia sum below ten. Extract a flat list of all individual ammonia readings from the valid tanks, filter out readings that are zero, and multiply all non-zero readings together. Return an array with the highest ammonia tank identifier, the found tank identifier, the boolean check result, and the product of non-zero readings.

title: Tidal Power Generator Efficiency
spec: Design `calculate(generators)` for ocean energy analysis. Each generator object contains a coastal site, a blade length, and a list of water velocity measurements. Filter out generators with a blade length less than five meters. Transform each to a summary with the coastal site and the total kinetic energy, calculated by squaring each velocity measurement and summing the results. Sort the summaries by total kinetic energy descending. Find the coastal site of the first summary with energy exceeding fifty thousand, and check if some summaries have energy below one thousand. Gather all water velocity measurements from the valid generators into one flat list, filter the list to keep velocities above ten, and sum these high velocity measurements. Return an array with the top coastal site, the found coastal site, the boolean result, and the high velocity sum.

title: Bonsai Tree Pruning Schedule
spec: Create `schedule(trees)` to manage botanical care. Each tree object features a species name, a tree age, and a list of branch growth lengths in centimeters. Discard trees younger than three years. Map each to a summary containing the species name and the total growth length obtained by summing the branch lengths. Sort the summaries by total growth length descending. Find the species name of the first tree with total growth exceeding fifty centimeters, and verify if all summaries have a total growth of at least ten centimeters. Extract all branch growth lengths from valid trees into a flat list, filter the list for lengths greater than five, and calculate the average of these long branches. Return an array containing the fastest growing species, the found species, the verification boolean, and the average long branch length.

title: Vintage Watch Movement Calibration
spec: Develop `calibrate(movements)` for horology adjustments. Each movement object has a serial number, a jewel count, and a list of timing variations in seconds. Filter out movements with a jewel count below seventeen. Transform each to a summary with the serial number and the average timing variation. Sort the summaries by the absolute value of the average variation in ascending order so the most accurate is first. Find the serial number of the first summary with an average variation exactly equal to zero, and check if some summaries have an average variation greater than twenty. Flatten all timing variations from the valid movements into a single list, filter out any timing variations that are zero, and sum the absolute values of the non-zero variations. Return an array containing the most accurate serial number, the found serial number, the boolean result, and the sum of absolute variations.

title: Seagrass Meadow Restoration
spec: Write a function `assess(meadows)` to track marine vegetation. Each meadow object includes a sector code, a water depth, and a list of shoot density counts. Discard meadows with a water depth greater than twenty meters. Map the remaining items to summaries containing the sector code and the minimum shoot density from the list of counts. Sort the summaries by minimum shoot density ascending. Find the sector code of the first summary with a minimum density below five, and check if all summaries have a minimum density of at least one. Extract a flat list of all shoot density counts from valid meadows, filter for density counts above fifty, and calculate the total sum of these high density counts. Return an array with the lowest density sector code, the found sector code, the boolean check, and the total high density sum.

title: Soundscape Ecology Monitor
spec: Implement `monitor(recordings)` to analyze environmental audio. Each recording object features a habitat region, a duration in minutes, and a list of bird call frequencies detected. Filter out recordings with a duration under ten minutes. Transform each to a summary with the habitat region and the count of unique bird call frequencies. Sort the summaries by the unique frequency count descending. Find the habitat region of the first summary with more than twenty unique frequencies, and check if some summaries have zero unique frequencies. Flatten all bird call frequencies from valid recordings into one list, filter the list to keep frequencies above two thousand hertz, and calculate the average of these high pitch frequencies. Return an array containing the most diverse habitat region, the found habitat region, the boolean result, and the average high pitch frequency.

title: Fossil Excavation Grid Tracker
spec: Design `track(grids)` to summarize paleontological digs. Each grid object contains a square identifier, an excavation depth, and a list of bone fragment weights. Discard grids where excavation depth is less than two meters. Map the valid grids to summaries containing the square identifier and the total weight of fragments. Sort the summaries by total weight descending. Find the square identifier of the first summary with a total weight over one hundred grams, and verify if all summaries have a total weight greater than zero. Extract a flat list of all bone fragment weights from the valid grids, filter for fragment weights exactly equal to ten, and sum these specific fragment weights. Return an array with the heaviest square identifier, the found square identifier, the verification boolean, and the sum of ten gram fragments.

title: Neon Sign Gas Mixture Calculator
spec: Create `calculate(tubes)` to optimize lighting manufacturing. Each tube object features a color name, a glass diameter, and a list of gas pressure readings. Filter out tubes with a glass diameter under eight millimeters. Transform each to a summary with the color name and the average gas pressure. Sort the summaries by average gas pressure ascending. Find the color name of the first summary with an average pressure below twelve, and check if some summaries have an average pressure above twenty. Combine all gas pressure readings from valid tubes into a single list, filter the list for pressures between fourteen and sixteen inclusive, and sum these optimal pressure readings. Return an array containing the lowest pressure color name, the found color name, the boolean result, and the sum of optimal pressures.

title: Kombucha Fermentation Monitor
spec: Develop `monitor(batches)` to track brewing progress. Each batch object includes a flavor profile, a brewing temperature, and a list of daily acidity levels. Discard batches brewed at a temperature below twenty degrees. Map each remaining batch to a summary with the flavor profile and the final acidity level, determined by finding the maximum value in the daily acidity list. Sort the summaries by final acidity level descending. Find the flavor profile of the first summary with a final acidity over four point five, and check if all summaries have a final acidity of at least three. Extract a flat list of all daily acidity levels from valid batches, filter for levels strictly less than three point five, and calculate the average of these early stage acidity levels. Return an array with the most acidic flavor profile, the found flavor profile, the boolean check, and the average early stage acidity.

title: Textile Thread Tension Tester
spec: Write a function `test(threads)` to evaluate fabric strength. Each thread object has a material type, a thread thickness, and a list of breakage tension weights. Filter out threads with a thickness less than zero point five millimeters. Transform them to summaries containing the material type and the average breakage tension. Sort the summaries by average breakage tension descending. Find the material type of the first summary with an average tension over fifty kilograms, and check if some summaries have an average tension below ten kilograms. Flatten all breakage tension weights from valid threads into one sequence, filter the sequence for weights above forty, and sum these high tension weights. Return an array containing the strongest material type, the found material type, the boolean result, and the sum of high tension weights.

title: Equestrian Show Jumping Faults
spec: Implement `score(rounds)` to tabulate sporting results. Each round object contains a rider name, a horse age, and a list of penalty points from each obstacle. Discard rounds where the horse age is under seven years. Map each round to a summary with the rider name and the total penalty points accumulated. Sort the summaries by total penalty points ascending so the fewest points are first. Find the rider name of the first summary with exactly zero penalty points, and verify if all summaries have total penalty points under twenty. Combine all individual penalty points from valid rounds into a flat list, filter the list to keep only penalty points of exactly four, and sum these knockdown penalty points. Return an array with the winning rider name, the found perfect rider name, the verification boolean, and the sum of knockdown penalties.

title: Beekeeping Wax Yield Estimator
spec: Design `estimate(hives)` to measure agricultural production. Each hive object features a colony name, a queen age in months, and a list of wax comb weights in grams collected over the season. Filter out hives where the queen age is over twenty four months. Transform each to a summary with the colony name and the total wax weight produced. Sort the summaries by total wax weight descending. Find the colony name of the first summary producing over one thousand grams of wax, and check if some summaries produced less than five hundred grams. Extract a flat list of all wax comb weights from valid hives, filter out weights below fifty grams, and calculate the average weight of these large wax combs. Return an array containing the top producing colony name, the found colony name, the boolean result, and the average large comb weight.

title: Elevator Cable Wear Inspector
spec: Create `inspect(cables)` for safety compliance. Each cable object includes a building zone, a cable diameter, and a list of tension loss percentages recorded over months. Discard cables with a diameter under fifteen millimeters. Map each to a summary containing the building zone and the maximum tension loss percentage found in its list. Sort the summaries by maximum tension loss descending. Find the building zone of the first summary with a tension loss over ten percent, and check if all summaries have a maximum tension loss below fifteen percent. Flatten all tension loss percentages from valid cables into a single list, filter the list for percentages strictly greater than five, and sum these significant tension loss percentages. Return an array with the worst wear building zone, the found building zone, the boolean check, and the sum of significant losses.

title: Violin Acoustic Resonance
spec: Develop `measure(violins)` to analyze musical instruments. Each violin object has a maker name, a wood age, and a list of resonance decibel peaks. Filter out violins with a wood age less than fifty years. Transform them to summaries containing the maker name and the average of the resonance decibel peaks. Sort the summaries by average decibel peak descending. Find the maker name of the first summary with an average peak over eighty decibels, and verify if some summaries have an average peak below sixty decibels. Combine all resonance decibel peaks from valid violins into one sequence, filter out peaks below seventy decibels, and sum these high resonance peaks. Return an array containing the loudest maker name, the found maker name, the verification boolean, and the sum of high resonance peaks.

title: Cave Stalactite Growth
spec: Write a function `project(formations)` to estimate geological progress. Each formation object features a cavern chamber, a current length, and a list of annual mineral drip rates in millimeters. Discard formations with a current length under one hundred millimeters. Map each to a summary with the cavern chamber and the projected total length, calculated by adding the sum of the annual drip rates to the current length. Sort the summaries by projected total length descending. Find the cavern chamber of the first summary with a projected length over five hundred millimeters, and check if all summaries have a projected length greater than two hundred. Extract a flat list of all annual mineral drip rates from valid formations, filter the list to keep rates above zero point five millimeters, and calculate the average of these fast drip rates. Return an array with the longest projected cavern chamber, the found cavern chamber, the boolean result, and the average fast drip rate.

title: Hot Air Balloon Buoyancy
spec: Implement `evaluate(flights)` for aviation testing. Each flight object contains a pilot name, an envelope volume, and a list of burner temperature intervals. Filter out flights with an envelope volume under two thousand cubic meters. Transform each to a summary containing the pilot name and the maximum burner temperature achieved. Sort the summaries by maximum burner temperature descending. Find the pilot name of the first summary with a temperature exceeding one hundred twenty degrees, and check if some summaries have a maximum temperature below ninety degrees. Flatten all burner temperature intervals from valid flights into a single list, filter the list for temperatures exactly equal to one hundred degrees, and sum these optimal temperatures. Return an array with the hottest flight pilot name, the found pilot name, the boolean check, and the sum of optimal temperatures.

title: Snowplow Route Clearance
spec: Design `clear(routes)` to manage winter logistics. Each route object includes a district name, a priority level, and a list of street snow depths in inches. Discard routes with a priority level lower than three. Map the remaining routes to summaries containing the district name and the total snow volume, found by summing the street snow depths. Sort the summaries by total snow volume descending. Find the district name of the first summary with a total volume over fifty inches, and verify if all summaries have a total volume of at least ten inches. Gather all street snow depths from valid routes into one flat list, filter the list to keep depths greater than eight inches, and calculate the total sum of these deep snow measurements. Return an array containing the heaviest snow district name, the found district name, the verification boolean, and the total deep snow sum.

title: Competitive Marching Band Scores
spec: Write a function `rank(performances)` that processes competition data. Each performance provides a band name, a list of numeric judge scores, and penalty points. First, calculate the average judge score for each band by dropping the highest and lowest scores. Then, subtract the penalty points from this average to find the final score. Filter out any bands whose final score falls below sixty. Finally, sort the remaining bands in descending order of their final scores and return a list of formatted strings combining the band name and final score. Example input: a performance by the Tigers with scores eight, nine, seven, and penalty one. The output list would contain a string like Tigers scored seven.

title: State Bridge Inspections
spec: Implement a function `prioritize(bridges)` to analyze infrastructure data. Each bridge record includes an identifier, daily traffic volume, and three ratings out of ten for structural, deck, and substructure condition. Determine the overall condition of each bridge, which is the lowest of its three ratings. Calculate a repair priority score by subtracting the overall condition from ten, then multiplying by the daily traffic volume. Discard bridges that have an overall condition of seven or higher, as they are considered safe.
